3.65.s:
3.321
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
kva kāle karmaṇā kena prāpnuvanti narottamāḥ..
tattvamasmākamācakṣva tvaṃ hi sarvavidarhasi .. 1 ..
3.65.d:
3.321
॥ ऋषय ऊचुः ॥ ॥
क्व काले कर्मणा केन प्राप्नुवन्ति नरोत्तमाः॥
तत्त्वमस्माकमाचक्ष्व त्वं हि सर्वविदर्हसि ॥ 1 ॥
3.65.m: The sages said: / At what time and by what deed do best of men reach [which realms]? / Explain that reality to us, for you are omniscient, worthy [to instruct].

3.65.s:
.. haṃsa uvāca .. ..
jyeṣṭhasvasāraṃ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ gurumeva ca ..
nityaṃ sampūjayedbhaktyā yāmyaloke mahīyate .. 2 ..
3.65.d:
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
ज्येष्ठस्वसारं पितरं मातरं गुरुमेव च ॥
नित्यं सम्पूजयेद्भक्त्या याम्यलोके महीयते ॥ 2 ॥
3.65.m: Haṃsa said: / If one constantly honours with devotion elder sister, father, mother, and teacher, / he is exalted in the realm of Yama.

3.65.s:
bhojanācchādanādyena tvatithiṃ caiva pūjayet ..
rājarājasya lokeṣu modate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 3 ..
3.65.d:
भोजनाच्छादनाद्येन त्वतिथिं चैव पूजयेत् ॥
राजराजस्य लोकेषु मोदते नात्र संशयः ॥ 3 ॥
3.65.m: And if one honours a guest with food, clothing, and the like, / he rejoices in the worlds of the king of kings; herein there is no doubt.

3.65.s:
meroḥ samīpaṃ gacchanvai nityādhyayanatatparaḥ ..
sudarśanā yatra ca sā jambūḥ khyātā dvijātayaḥ .. 4 ..
3.65.d:
मेरोः समीपं गच्छन्वै नित्याध्ययनतत्परः ॥
सुदर्शना यत्र च सा जम्बूः ख्याता द्विजातयः ॥ 4 ॥
3.65.m: Devoted to continual study, he goes near to Meru / where the famous rose-apple tree named Sudarśanā is, O twice-born ones.

3.65.s:
nṛtte gīte ca kuśalaṃ nandanaṃ yānti te vanam ..
himāni vṛttā gacchanti tathā caivottarānkurūn .. 5 ..
3.65.d:
नृत्ते गीते च कुशलं नन्दनं यान्ति ते वनम् ॥
हिमानि वृत्ता गच्छन्ति तथा चैवोत्तरान्कुरून् ॥ 5 ॥
3.65.m: Those skilled in dance and song go to the Nandana grove; / those who endure frost go likewise to Uttarakuru.

3.65.s:
nityaṃ dānaparāḥ santo lokaṃ gacchanti śāśvatam ..
ādityalokaṃ gacchanti tathā ye tapasi sthitāḥ .. 6 ..
3.65.d:
नित्यं दानपराः सन्तो लोकं गच्छन्ति शाश्वतम् ॥
आदित्यलोकं गच्छन्ति तथा ये तपसि स्थिताः ॥ 6 ॥
3.65.m: Those who are good, constantly devoted to generosity, go to the eternal world; / likewise, those established in asceticism go to the realm of the sun.

3.65.s:
tīrthayātrāparā yānti tathā lokaṃ pracetasaḥ ..
saṃgrāme nihatā yānti śakralokamasaṃśayam .. 7 ..
3.65.d:
तीर्थयात्रापरा यान्ति तथा लोकं प्रचेतसः ॥
संग्रामे निहता यान्ति शक्रलोकमसंशयम् ॥ 7 ॥
3.65.m: Those devoted to pilgrimages to sacred places go likewise to the realm of Varuṇa; / those slain in battle go to the realm of Śakra without doubt.

3.65.s:
prājāpatyaṃ tathā yāṃti samyagvṛtvā mahīkṣitaḥ ..
gavāṃ patyā tathā yāṃti golokaṃ mānavottamāḥ .. 8 ..
3.65.d:
प्राजापत्यं तथा यांति सम्यग्वृत्वा महीक्षितः ॥
गवां पत्या तथा यांति गोलोकं मानवोत्तमाः ॥ 8 ॥
3.65.m: Kings, having governed properly, go to the realm of Prajāpati; / by protecting cattle, the best of men go to the realm of cows.

3.65.s:
yānti lokaṃ ca sūryasya nityaṃ ye satyabhāṣiṇaḥ..
pratigrahānnivṛttāśca vasūnāmapi mānavāḥ .. 9 ..
3.65.d:
यान्ति लोकं च सूर्यस्य नित्यं ये सत्यभाषिणः॥
प्रतिग्रहान्निवृत्ताश्च वसूनामपि मानवाः ॥ 9 ॥
3.65.m: Those who constantly speak truth go to the realm of the sun; / and men turned away from acceptance of gifts go to the realm of the Vasus.

3.65.s:
vāyuloke mahīyante rogiṇāṃ paricārakāḥ ..
lokaṃ gacchantyathāgneyaṃ vahniśuśrūṣaṇe ratāḥ .. 3.321.10 ...
3.65.d:
वायुलोके महीयन्ते रोगिणां परिचारकाः ॥
लोकं गच्छन्त्यथाग्नेयं वह्निशुश्रूषणे रताः ॥ 3.321.10 ॥।
3.65.m: Caretakers of the sick are exalted in the realm of Vāyu; / those delighting in service to the fire go to the fire-god's realm.

3.65.s:
yāṃti te nairṛtaṃ lokaṃ prapārakṣaṇatatparāḥ ..
bhṛgūṇāmapi lokeṣu modantyākāśaśāyinaḥ .. 11 ..
3.65.d:
यांति ते नैरृतं लोकं प्रपारक्षणतत्पराः ॥
भृगूणामपि लोकेषु मोदन्त्याकाशशायिनः ॥ 11 ॥
3.65.m: Those devoted to protecting cisterns go to the realm of Nirṛti; / those who sleep under the open sky rejoice in the worlds of the Bhṛgus.

3.65.s:
yāṃti cāṅgirasaṃ lokaṃ vratenānena mānavāḥ ..
marutāṃ ca tathā lokaṃ yāṃti yānapradā narāḥ .. 12 ..
3.65.d:
यांति चाङ्गिरसं लोकं व्रतेनानेन मानवाः ॥
मरुतां च तथा लोकं यांति यानप्रदा नराः ॥ 12 ॥
3.65.m: Through this vow, men go to the realm of the Aṅgirases; / and men who donate conveyances go to the realm of the Maruts.

3.65.s:
nāsatyaloke modante tathaivauṣadhadāyinaḥ ..
rudralokaṃ prapadyante govipranaravatsalāḥ ..13 ...
3.65.d:
नासत्यलोके मोदन्ते तथैवौषधदायिनः ॥
रुद्रलोकं प्रपद्यन्ते गोविप्रनरवत्सलाः ॥13 ॥।
3.65.m: Those who give medicine rejoice in the realm of the Nāsatya twins; / those fond of cattle, brahmins, and people reach the realm of Rudra.

3.65.s:
svācāraniratā yāṃti vaiśvadevamasaṃśayam ..
ādityaiḥ saha modaṃte dayāvantastu ye narāḥ .. 14 ..
3.65.d:
स्वाचारनिरता यांति वैश्वदेवमसंशयम् ॥
आदित्यैः सह मोदंते दयावन्तस्तु ये नराः ॥ 14 ॥
3.65.m: Those devoted to correct conduct go to the realm of the Viśvedevas without doubt; / and men who are compassionate rejoice together with the Ādityas.

3.65.s:
brahmalokaṃ viṣṇulokaṃ rudralokaṃ tathaiva ca ..
tadbhaktaireva labhyante nānyathā dvijasattamāḥ..15..
3.65.d:
ब्रह्मलोकं विष्णुलोकं रुद्रलोकं तथैव च ॥
तद्भक्तैरेव लभ्यन्ते नान्यथा द्विजसत्तमाः॥15॥
3.65.m: The world of Brahmā, the world of Viṣṇu, and likewise the world of Rudra / are attained only by their devotees, not otherwise, O best of the twice-born.

3.65.s:
yasya devasya yo bhaktiṃ sadā vahati mānavaḥ..
sampadastasya sālokyaṃ yāṃti nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ..16..
3.65.d:
यस्य देवस्य यो भक्तिं सदा वहति मानवः॥
सम्पदस्तस्य सालोक्यं यांति नास्त्यत्र संशयः॥16॥
3.65.m: Whatever deity a man constantly holds devotion for, / upon their prosperity they attain shared realm with that deity; herein there is no doubt.

3.65.s:
lokeṣu divyeṣu gatirmayoktā karmānurūpā puruṣasya viprāḥ ..
ataḥ paraṃ kiṃ kathayāmyahaṃ vai tanme gadadhvaṃ tapasi pradhānāḥ .. 17 ..
3.322
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
kathayasvāmitaprājña strīṇāṃ dharmamataḥ param ..
tadvayaṃ śrotumicchāmastvaṃ hi sarvaviducyase .. 1 ..
.. haṃsa uvāca ..
strīdharmaḥ pūrva evāyaṃ vivāhe bandhubhiḥ kṛtaḥ ..
sadharmacāriṇī bharturbhavedagnisamīpataḥ..2..
susvabhāvā suvimanā suvibhaktā sudarśanā ..
ananyacittā sumukhī bhartussā dharmacāriṇī .. 3 ..
putravaktramivābhīkṣṇaṃ bharturvadanamīkṣatī ..
yā sādhvī niyatācārā sā bhaveddharmacāriṇī .. 4 ..
śrutvedaṃ patidharmaṃ vai mahāśramakṛtaṃ śivam ..
yā bhaveddharmaparamā nārī bhartṛsamavratā..5..
devavatsatataṃ sādhvī bhartāramanupaśyati..
śuśrūṣāṃ paricaryāñca devatulyaṃ prakurvatī ..6..
3.65.d:
लोकेषु दिव्येषु गतिर्मयोक्ता कर्मानुरूपा पुरुषस्य विप्राः ॥
अतः परं किं कथयाम्यहं वै तन्मे गदध्वं तपसि प्रधानाः ॥ 17 ॥
3.322
॥ ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
कथयस्वामितप्राज्ञ स्त्रीणां धर्ममतः परम् ॥
तद्वयं श्रोतुमिच्छामस्त्वं हि सर्वविदुच्यसे ॥ 1 ॥
॥ हंस उवाच ॥
स्त्रीधर्मः पूर्व एवायं विवाहे बन्धुभिः कृतः ॥
सधर्मचारिणी भर्तुर्भवेदग्निसमीपतः॥2॥
सुस्वभावा सुविमना सुविभक्ता सुदर्शना ॥
अनन्यचित्ता सुमुखी भर्तुस्सा धर्मचारिणी ॥ 3 ॥
पुत्रवक्त्रमिवाभीक्ष्णं भर्तुर्वदनमीक्षती ॥
या साध्वी नियताचारा सा भवेद्धर्मचारिणी ॥ 4 ॥
श्रुत्वेदं पतिधर्मं वै महाश्रमकृतं शिवम् ॥
या भवेद्धर्मपरमा नारी भर्तृसमव्रता॥5॥
देववत्सततं साध्वी भर्तारमनुपश्यति॥
शुश्रूषां परिचर्याञ्च देवतुल्यं प्रकुर्वती ॥6॥
3.65.m:
The departure of a person into heavenly realms according to their actions has been spoken by me, O brahmins; / what more shall I tell beyond this? Say that to me, O foremost in asceticism!
The sages said: / Speak, O one of boundless wisdom, on the dharma of women beyond this; / we wish to hear that, for you are called omniscient.
Haṃsa said: / This was established as the primary dharma of a woman by kinsmen at marriage: / in the presence of fire, she should be a partner in dharma with her husband.
Good-natured, well-disposed, well-proportioned, lovely to behold, / singular in mind, pleasant-faced: she is a partner in dharma with her husband.
Ever looking at her husband's face as if at the face of a son, / she who is virtuous and restrained in conduct is a partner in dharma.
Having heard this auspicious duty to the husband that requires great exertion, / a woman who is supremely devoted to dharma observes vows equal to her husband's.
A virtuous woman constantly looks upon her husband like a god, / rendering service and attendance as if to a deity.

3.65.s:
vaśyābhāvena sumanāḥ suvratā susamāhitā ..
ananyacittā sumanā bhartuḥ sā dharmabhāginī..7..
pāruṣyamapi voktā yā dṛṣṭā vā krūracakṣuṣā ..
suprasannamukhī bharturyā nārī sā pativratā..8..
na candrasūryau tadrūpaṃ nenau yā ca nirīkṣate..
bhartṛvarjaṃ varārohā sā bhaveddharmabhāginī..9..
daridraṃ vyādhitaṃ dīnaṃ cādhinā parikīrtitam ..
patimputramivārakṣetsā nārī dharmabhāginī .. 3.322.10 ..
yā nārī prayatā dakṣā yā nārī putriṇī bhavet ..
pativratā patiprāṇā sā nārī dharmabhāginī .. 11 ..
śuśrūṣāṃ paricaryāñca karotyavimanāḥ sadā ..
supratītā sumanāḥ sā nārī dharmabhāginī .. 12 ..
na kāmeṣu na bhogeṣu naiśvarye na sukhe tathā ..
spṛhā yasyā yathā bhartuḥ sā nārī dharmabhāginī .. 13 ..
kāmārthā na vratā nityaṃ gṛhaśuśrūṣaṇe ratā ..
susammṛṣṭakṣayā caiva gośakṛtkṛtalepanā .. 14 ..
3.65.d:
वश्याभावेन सुमनाः सुव्रता सुसमाहिता ॥
अनन्यचित्ता सुमना भर्तुः सा धर्मभागिनी॥7॥
पारुष्यमपि वोक्ता या दृष्टा वा क्रूरचक्षुषा ॥
सुप्रसन्नमुखी भर्तुर्या नारी सा पतिव्रता॥8॥
न चन्द्रसूर्यौ तद्रूपं नेनौ या च निरीक्षते॥
भर्तृवर्जं वरारोहा सा भवेद्धर्मभागिनी॥9॥
दरिद्रं व्याधितं दीनं चाधिना परिकीर्तितम् ॥
पतिम्पुत्रमिवारक्षेत्सा नारी धर्मभागिनी ॥ 3.322.10 ॥
या नारी प्रयता दक्षा या नारी पुत्रिणी भवेत् ॥
पतिव्रता पतिप्राणा सा नारी धर्मभागिनी ॥ 11 ॥
शुश्रूषां परिचर्याञ्च करोत्यविमनाः सदा ॥
सुप्रतीता सुमनाः सा नारी धर्मभागिनी ॥ 12 ॥
न कामेषु न भोगेषु नैश्वर्ये न सुखे तथा ॥
स्पृहा यस्या यथा भर्तुः सा नारी धर्मभागिनी ॥ 13 ॥
कामार्था न व्रता नित्यं गृहशुश्रूषणे रता ॥
सुसम्मृष्टक्षया चैव गोशकृत्कृतलेपना ॥ 14 ॥
3.65.m:
Well-disposed through submissiveness, faithful to vows, fully composed, / single-minded, and cheerful, she shares in the husband's dharma.
Even if addressed with harshness or looked at with a cruel eye, / the woman who has a serene face toward her husband is a devoted wife.
And she whose form neither the moon nor the sun beholds with their eye,
except her husband, that fair-hipped woman becomes a sharer in dharma.
Poor, diseased, wretched, or proclaimed to be afflicted by mental sorrow,
her husband she should protect as if he were her son; such a woman is a sharer in dharma.
The woman who is restrained, capable, and who has sons,
devoted to her husband, her husband being her very life, that woman is a sharer in dharma.
She who always renders obedience and service without despondency,
well-satisfied and cheerful of mind, that woman is a sharer in dharma.
Neither in desires, nor in enjoyments, nor in sovereignty, nor in pleasure
does she have longing as she has for her husband; that woman is a sharer in dharma.
Not desiring sensual pleasure, taking vows, constantly devoted to household service,
keeping her dwelling well swept and smeared with cow dung,

3.65.s:
agnikāryaparā nityaṃ sadā puṣpabalipradā ..
devatātithibhṛtyānāṃ nirūpya patinā saha .. 15 ..
śeṣānnamupabhuñjānā yathānyāyaṃ yathāvidhi ..
tuṣṭabhṛtyajanā nityaṃ nārīdharmeṇa yujyate .. 16 ..
śvaśrūśvaśurayoḥ pādām̐stoṣayantī guṇānvitā ..
mātāpitṛratā nityaṃ yā nārī sā tapodhanā .. 17 ..
3.65.d:
अग्निकार्यपरा नित्यं सदा पुष्पबलिप्रदा ॥
देवतातिथिभृत्यानां निरूप्य पतिना सह ॥ 15 ॥
शेषान्नमुपभुञ्जाना यथान्यायं यथाविधि ॥
तुष्टभृत्यजना नित्यं नारीधर्मेण युज्यते ॥ 16 ॥
श्वश्रूश्वशुरयोः पादाम्̐स्तोषयन्ती गुणान्विता ॥
मातापितृरता नित्यं या नारी सा तपोधना ॥ 17 ॥
3.65.m:
Constantly devoted to the ritual of the fire, always offering flowers and oblations,
having provided, together with her husband, for the deities, guests, and servants,
Consuming the remaining food according to rule and according to injunction,
always having satisfied her servants, she is joined with the dharma of women.
Pleasing the feet of her mother-in-law and father-in-law, endowed with virtues,
always devoted to her mother and father, that woman has asceticism as her wealth.

3.65.s:
brāhmaṇāndurbalānāthadīnāndhakṛpaṇām̐stathā ..
bibhartyanena yā nārī sā pativratabhāginī .. 18 ..
3.65.d:
ब्राह्मणान्दुर्बलानाथदीनान्धकृपणाम्̐स्तथा ॥
बिभर्त्यनेन या नारी सा पतिव्रतभागिनी ॥ 18 ॥
3.65.m:
Brahmins, the weak, the helpless, the wretched, the blind, and the miserable—
the woman who sustains these with food is a sharer in the virtue of devotion to her husband.

3.65.s:
vratañcarati yā nityaṃ duścaraṃ spaṣṭamānasā ..
paticittā patiratā sā pativratabhāginī .. 19 ..
3.65.d:
व्रतञ्चरति या नित्यं दुश्चरं स्पष्टमानसा ॥
पतिचित्ता पतिरता सा पतिव्रतभागिनी ॥ 19 ॥
3.65.m:
She who constantly performs a vow difficult to observe, with a clear mind,
her mind on her husband, devoted to her husband, is a sharer in the virtue of devotion to her husband.

3.65.s:
puṇyametattapaścaiva svargaścaiva sanātanaḥ ..
yā nārī bhartṛparamā bhavedbhartṛvatā śivā ..3.322.20..
3.65.d:
पुण्यमेतत्तपश्चैव स्वर्गश्चैव सनातनः ॥
या नारी भर्तृपरमा भवेद्भर्तृवता शिवा ॥3.322.20॥
3.65.m:
This is merit, this is asceticism, and this is eternal heaven,
when an auspicious woman, possessing a husband, holds her husband supreme.

3.65.s:
patirhi devo nārīṇāṃ patirbandhuḥ patirgatiḥ ..
patyā gatiḥ samā nāsti daivataṃ vā yathā patiḥ ..21..
3.65.d:
पतिर्हि देवो नारीणां पतिर्बन्धुः पतिर्गतिः ॥
पत्या गतिः समा नास्ति दैवतं वा यथा पतिः ॥21॥
3.65.m:
For a husband is the god of women; a husband is their kinsman; a husband is their refuge.
There is no refuge equal to a husband, nor any deity like a husband.

3.65.s:
patiḥ svargaprado nāryā yadā talpamanā bhavet ..
yadyatkāryamakāryaṃ vā yadi vā prāṇanāśanam .. 22 ..
3.65.d:
पतिः स्वर्गप्रदो नार्या यदा तल्पमना भवेत् ॥
यद्यत्कार्यमकार्यं वा यदि वा प्राणनाशनम् ॥ 22 ॥
3.65.m:
A husband bestows heaven upon a woman when he is disposed toward her bed,
whatever is to be done or not to be done, or even if it causes loss of life.

3.65.s:
patiḥ pātakayukto vā vyādhito vā kathañcana ..
āpanno ripusaṃstho vā brahmaśāpārdito'pi vā .. 23 ..
3.65.d:
पतिः पातकयुक्तो वा व्याधितो वा कथञ्चन ॥
आपन्नो रिपुसंस्थो वा ब्रह्मशापार्दितोऽपि वा ॥ 23 ॥
3.65.m:
Whether her husband is guilty of a crime, or diseased in some way,
fallen into misfortune, captive to an enemy, or afflicted by a brahmin's curse,

3.65.s:
āpaddharmānanuprekṣya tatkāryamaviśaṅkayā ..
svātaṃtryamuktamparamaṃ hi pāpaṃ strīṇāṃ sadā tena sadaiva nārī ..
svātantryahīnā satatambhaveddhi yā kāmayennākamitaścirāya .. 24 ..
3.323
.. haṃsa uvāca .. .. ..
svesve dharme vyavasthānaṃ varṇānāṃ pṛthivīpateḥ ..
paro dharmaḥ sadā proktastatra yatra bhavennaraḥ .. 1..
devabrāhmaṇagosādhvīsādhūnāmapi pūjanam ..
nigrahaścaiva duṣṭānānnṛpaterdharmakāraṇam .. 2 ..
samatā vyavahāreṣu svayañcaivānvavekṣaṇam ..
rājñāṃ dharmaṃ paraṃ vidyāttathā vai cāradṛṣṭitā .. 3 ..
svadeśapālanaṃ dharmaḥ pararāṣṭrābhimardanam ..
yajñadānakriyā caiva saṃgrāme cāpalāyanam .. 4 ..
mṛgayākṣā tathā pānaṃ garhitāni mahībhujām ..
vāgdaṇḍayostu pāruṣyantathaivārthasya dūṣaṇam .. 5 ..
3.65.d:
आपद्धर्माननुप्रेक्ष्य तत्कार्यमविशङ्कया ॥
स्वातंत्र्यमुक्तम्परमं हि पापं स्त्रीणां सदा तेन सदैव नारी ॥
स्वातन्त्र्यहीना सततम्भवेद्धि या कामयेन्नाकमितश्चिराय ॥ 24 ॥
3.323
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥ ॥
स्वेस्वे धर्मे व्यवस्थानं वर्णानां पृथिवीपतेः ॥
परो धर्मः सदा प्रोक्तस्तत्र यत्र भवेन्नरः ॥ 1॥
देवब्राह्मणगोसाध्वीसाधूनामपि पूजनम् ॥
निग्रहश्चैव दुष्टानान्नृपतेर्धर्मकारणम् ॥ 2 ॥
समता व्यवहारेषु स्वयञ्चैवान्ववेक्षणम् ॥
राज्ञां धर्मं परं विद्यात्तथा वै चारदृष्टिता ॥ 3 ॥
स्वदेशपालनं धर्मः परराष्ट्राभिमर्दनम् ॥
यज्ञदानक्रिया चैव संग्रामे चापलायनम् ॥ 4 ॥
मृगयाक्षा तथा पानं गर्हितानि महीभुजाम् ॥
वाग्दण्डयोस्तु पारुष्यन्तथैवार्थस्य दूषणम् ॥ 5 ॥
3.65.m:
Having observed the duties of adversity, that must be done without hesitation.
For independence is proclaimed to be the supreme sin for women; therefore, a woman always / must remain ever free from independence, if she desires heaven for a long time hereafter.
Haṃsa said:
Remaining established in their respective dharmas by the castes is for a lord of the earth
always proclaimed to be the highest dharma, wherever a man may be.
Worship of the gods, brahmins, cows, virtuous women, and holy men,
and the suppression of the wicked, is the source of dharma for a king.
Impartiality in legal proceedings and personal investigation—
one should know this as the supreme dharma of kings, as well as viewing through spies.
Protecting his own realm is dharma, as is subduing enemy kingdoms,
performing sacrifices and giving gifts, and not fleeing from battle.
Hunting, dice, and drinking are condemned for kings,
as are harshness of speech and punishment, and likewise corrupting wealth.

3.65.s:
sandhivigrahadānānāmāsanasya tathaiva ca ..
dvaidhībhāvasya cāpyuktā sevā vai saṃśrayasya ca .. 6 ..
jñātvā kālañcalaṃ rājā ṣāḍguṇyasya hi niścaye ..
indriyāṇāñjaye yatnaḥ sadā syāddvijapuṅgavāḥ .. 7 ..
tato bhṛtyajayaḥ kāryaḥ samastavijayastataḥ ..
kāmaḥ krodho mado lobho māno harṣastathaiva ca .. 8 ..
ābhyantarā vijetavyā ripavaḥ ṣaṇmahībhujā ..
tatastu śatravo jeyāḥ kulyāścetarakṛtrimāḥ ..9..
bhūmimitrahiraṇyānāmarjjane yatnavānbhavet ..
dharmārthakāmasevā ca sadā kāryā mahīkṣitā .. 3.323.10 ..
svāmyamātyañjanaṃ durgaṃ kośo daṇḍaḥ suhṛttathā ..
rājye prakṛtayaḥ sapta rakṣyā yatnena bhūbhujā .. 11 ..
daivamantraprabhūtsāhaśaktiyuktastathā bhavet ..
maṅgalācārayuktānāṃ sidhyante devaśaktayaḥ .. 12 ..
3.65.d:
सन्धिविग्रहदानानामासनस्य तथैव च ॥
द्वैधीभावस्य चाप्युक्ता सेवा वै संश्रयस्य च ॥ 6 ॥
ज्ञात्वा कालञ्चलं राजा षाड्गुण्यस्य हि निश्चये ॥
इन्द्रियाणाञ्जये यत्नः सदा स्याद्द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥ 7 ॥
ततो भृत्यजयः कार्यः समस्तविजयस्ततः ॥
कामः क्रोधो मदो लोभो मानो हर्षस्तथैव च ॥ 8 ॥
आभ्यन्तरा विजेतव्या रिपवः षण्महीभुजा ॥
ततस्तु शत्रवो जेयाः कुल्याश्चेतरकृत्रिमाः ॥9॥
भूमिमित्रहिरण्यानामर्ज्जने यत्नवान्भवेत् ॥
धर्मार्थकामसेवा च सदा कार्या महीक्षिता ॥ 3.323.10 ॥
स्वाम्यमात्यञ्जनं दुर्गं कोशो दण्डः सुहृत्तथा ॥
राज्ये प्रकृतयः सप्त रक्ष्या यत्नेन भूभुजा ॥ 11 ॥
दैवमन्त्रप्रभूत्साहशक्तियुक्तस्तथा भवेत् ॥
मङ्गलाचारयुक्तानां सिध्यन्ते देवशक्तयः ॥ 12 ॥
3.65.m:
Peace, war, marching, and encamping,
and taking recourse to dual policy and alliance are declared.
Knowing the shifting time in determining the sixfold foreign policy,
O bull-like twice-borns, there should always be effort in conquering the senses by the king.
Then the conquest of servants should be made, and then the conquest of everything.
Desire, anger, pride, greed, arrogance, and likewise joy—
These six internal enemies must be conquered by a king.
Then the enemies belonging to one's own family and those that are natural or artificial are to be conquered.
He should be diligent in the acquisition of land, allies, and gold;
and the cultivation of dharma, wealth, and pleasure must always be pursued by a ruler of the earth.
The sovereign, the minister, the people, the fortress, the treasury, the army, and the ally—
these seven constituents in a kingdom must be protected with effort by the king.
He should likewise be endowed with the powers of fate, counsel, lordship, and energy;
for those who possess auspicious conduct, the powers of the gods succeed.

3.65.s:
caturaṅgabalaṃ kuryātsubhṛtañca tathā nṛpaḥ ..
karmaṇā manasā vācā sadā lokaṃ prasādayet .. 13..
mahaccāvaraṇaṃ kāryannityameva samṛddhaye ..
rājā sahāyasampannaḥ paśavyañjāṅgalaṃ śivam..14..
vaiśyaśūdrajanaprāyamarogaṃ deśamāvaseta..
tatra durgāṇi kurvīta svadurgañca viśeṣavat .. 15 ..
dhanvadurgammahīdurgaṃ giridurgantathaiva ca ..
adurgaṃ vṛkṣadurgañca naradurgantathaiva ca .. 16 ..
eṣāmanyatame durge dhanadhānyasamāyute ..
hastyaśvarathasampanne maṇibhīrūpaśobhite .. 17 ..
pattyāḍhye yodhabahule yuddhopakaraṇairyute ..
susañcite dhanāḍhye ca bahupeye bahūdake .. 18 ..
hastyaśvanaragovaidyasāṃvatsarayute śubhe ..
ghṛtatailauṣadhiyute sarvopakaraṇaistathā .. 19 ..
prākāraparikhāvapragopurāṭṭālakairyute ..
pāpataskaradurvṛttakruddhalubdhādivarjite..3.323.20..
3.65.d:
चतुरङ्गबलं कुर्यात्सुभृतञ्च तथा नृपः ॥
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा सदा लोकं प्रसादयेत् ॥ 13॥
महच्चावरणं कार्यन्नित्यमेव समृद्धये ॥
राजा सहायसम्पन्नः पशव्यञ्जाङ्गलं शिवम्॥14॥
वैश्यशूद्रजनप्रायमरोगं देशमावसेत॥
तत्र दुर्गाणि कुर्वीत स्वदुर्गञ्च विशेषवत् ॥ 15 ॥
धन्वदुर्गम्महीदुर्गं गिरिदुर्गन्तथैव च ॥
अदुर्गं वृक्षदुर्गञ्च नरदुर्गन्तथैव च ॥ 16 ॥
एषामन्यतमे दुर्गे धनधान्यसमायुते ॥
हस्त्यश्वरथसम्पन्ने मणिभीरूपशोभिते ॥ 17 ॥
पत्त्याढ्ये योधबहुले युद्धोपकरणैर्युते ॥
सुसञ्चिते धनाढ्ये च बहुपेये बहूदके ॥ 18 ॥
हस्त्यश्वनरगोवैद्यसांवत्सरयुते शुभे ॥
घृततैलौषधियुते सर्वोपकरणैस्तथा ॥ 19 ॥
प्राकारपरिखावप्रगोपुराट्टालकैर्युते ॥
पापतस्करदुर्वृत्तक्रुद्धलुब्धादिवर्जिते॥3.323.20॥
3.65.m:
The king should establish a fourfold army and keep it well-maintained;
by deed, mind, and speech, he should always gladden the world.
A great enclosure should constantly be made for prosperity.
A king, well-supplied with allies, [should dwell in] an auspicious wilderness suitable for cattle,
He should inhabit a disease-free country consisting mostly of vaiśyas and śūdras.
There he should build fortresses, and especially his own fortress:
A desert fortress, an earthen fortress, and likewise a hill fortress,
a water fortress, a forest fortress, and likewise a human fortress.
In any one of these fortresses, supplied with wealth and grain,
endowed with elephants, horses, and chariots, adorned with gems and fearlessness,
Abundant in infantry, full of warriors, equipped with implements of war,
well-provisioned, rich in wealth, with much to drink and plenty of water,
Endowed with physicians for elephants, horses, men, and cows, and with astrologers, auspicious,
provided with ghee, oil, and medicinal herbs, and likewise with all implements,
Supplied with ramparts, moats, earthworks, gatehouses, and watchtowers,
free from sinners, thieves, the ill-behaved, the angry, the greedy, and the like,

3.65.s:
daivajñasthapatibhyāntu saṃmatyā śubhalakṣaṇam ..
tatrāvasetsvayaṃ rājā sarvopakaraṇairyutam .. 21 ..
kulīnāṃ rūpasampannāṃ savarṇāñca narādhipaḥ ..
kuryādbhāryāṃ suśīlāñca vinītāṃ dharmavatsalām .. 22 ..
tayā saha sadā rājā gṛhasthāśramacoditam ..
pañcayajñavidhānantu kārayeta purohitam .. 23 ..
yajecca vividhairyajñaiḥ pūjayeddevatāstathā ..
devatāyatanānkūpāṃstaḍāgāṃścaiva kārayet .. .. 24 ..
3.65.d:
दैवज्ञस्थपतिभ्यान्तु संमत्या शुभलक्षणम् ॥
तत्रावसेत्स्वयं राजा सर्वोपकरणैर्युतम् ॥ 21 ॥
कुलीनां रूपसम्पन्नां सवर्णाञ्च नराधिपः ॥
कुर्याद्भार्यां सुशीलाञ्च विनीतां धर्मवत्सलाम् ॥ 22 ॥
तया सह सदा राजा गृहस्थाश्रमचोदितम् ॥
पञ्चयज्ञविधानन्तु कारयेत पुरोहितम् ॥ 23 ॥
यजेच्च विविधैर्यज्ञैः पूजयेद्देवतास्तथा ॥
देवतायतनान्कूपांस्तडागांश्चैव कारयेत् ॥ ॥ 24 ॥
3.65.m:
Having auspicious marks, with the approval of an astrologer and an architect,
there the king should dwell in person, equipped with all provisions.
Of noble family, endowed with beauty, of the same caste,
well-behaved, modest, and fond of dharma—such a wife the ruler of men should take.
Together with her, the king should constantly cause the domestic priest
to perform the rite of the five great sacrifices prescribed for the householder stage of life.
He should sacrifice with various sacrifices, and likewise worship the deities;
he should cause temples, wells, and tanks to be constructed,

3.65.s:
udyānāni vicitrāṇi gobrāhmaṇagṛhāṇi ca ..
duṣṭadaṇḍaḥ satāmpūjā dharmeṇa ca dhanārjanam .. 25 ..
3.65.d:
उद्यानानि विचित्राणि गोब्राह्मणगृहाणि च ॥
दुष्टदण्डः सताम्पूजा धर्मेण च धनार्जनम् ॥ 25 ॥
3.65.m:
Wonderful gardens, and dwellings for cows and brahmins.
Punishing the wicked, honoring the virtuous, and acquiring wealth through dharma,

3.65.s:
rāṣṭrarakṣā samatvañca vyavahāreṣu pañcakam ..
bhūmipānāmmahāyajñāḥ sarvakalmaṣanāśanāḥ .. 26 ..
3.65.d:
राष्ट्ररक्षा समत्वञ्च व्यवहारेषु पञ्चकम् ॥
भूमिपानाम्महायज्ञाः सर्वकल्मषनाशनाः ॥ 26 ॥
3.65.m:
Protection of the realm, and impartiality in legal proceedings—these five
are the great sacrifices of kings, destroying all impurities.

3.65.s:
gaṇaṃ lakṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ turagañcābhiṣecayet ..
salakṣaṇaṃ tathā ratnaṃ khaḍgakambibhṛyānnṛpaḥ .. 27 ..
3.65.d:
गणं लक्षणसंयुक्तं तुरगञ्चाभिषेचयेत् ॥
सलक्षणं तथा रत्नं खड्गकम्बिभृयान्नृपः ॥ 27 ॥
3.65.m:
The king should inaugurate an auspicious herd and a horse;
and he should bear auspicious jewels, a sword, and a bow.

3.65.s:
durgasthaśca niyuñjīta grāmegrāme ca pālakān ..
daśagrāmādhipāṃścānyaṃ śatagrāmādhipāṃstathā .. 28 ..
3.65.d:
दुर्गस्थश्च नियुञ्जीत ग्रामेग्रामे च पालकान् ॥
दशग्रामाधिपांश्चान्यं शतग्रामाधिपांस्तथा ॥ 28 ॥
3.65.m: Stationed in a fortress, he should appoint protectors in every village, / and others as lords of ten villages, and likewise lords of a hundred villages.

3.65.s:
deśeśvarāṃstathā kuryānnagarasthānviśeṣataḥ ..
grāmadoṣānsamutpannān grāmapālaḥ śamaṃ nayet .. 29 ..
3.65.d:
देशेश्वरांस्तथा कुर्यान्नगरस्थान्विशेषतः ॥
ग्रामदोषान्समुत्पन्नान् ग्रामपालः शमं नयेत् ॥ 29 ॥
3.65.m: He should likewise appoint lords of regions, especially those stationed in cities. / The village protector should pacify wrongs that have arisen in a village.

3.65.s:
aśaktaśca daśeśāya sa tu gatvā nivedayet ..
śateśāya daśeśastu śateśo deśapāya ca ..3.323.30..
3.65.d:
अशक्तश्च दशेशाय स तु गत्वा निवेदयेत् ॥
शतेशाय दशेशस्तु शतेशो देशपाय च ॥3.323.30॥
3.65.m: If unable, he should go and report to the lord of ten; / and the lord of ten to the lord of a hundred, and the lord of a hundred to the regional protector.

3.65.s:
grāmādipālakānāṃ tu śaucāśaucaṃ narādhipaḥ ..
cāraiḥ suviditaṃ kuryājjñātvā duṣṭāṃśca ghātayet .. 31 ..
3.65.d:
ग्रामादिपालकानां तु शौचाशौचं नराधिपः ॥
चारैः सुविदितं कुर्याज्ज्ञात्वा दुष्टांश्च घातयेत् ॥ 31 ॥
3.65.m: The ruler of men should make the purity or impurity of protectors of villages and the rest / well known through spies, and having learned of corrupt ones, he should have them executed.

3.65.s:
rājño hi rakṣādhikṛtāḥ parasvādāyinaḥ śaṭhāḥ ..
bhṛtyā bhavanti prāyeṇa tebhyo rakṣedvasundharām ..32 ..
3.65.d:
राज्ञो हि रक्षाधिकृताः परस्वादायिनः शठाः ॥
भृत्या भवन्ति प्रायेण तेभ्यो रक्षेद्वसुन्धराम् ॥32 ॥
3.65.m: For royal officers in charge of protection are generally rogue servants / who seize others' property; from them he should protect the earth.

3.65.s:
tathā ca rakṣādhikṛtānanurūpeṇa yojayet ..
vibhavena dvija śreṣṭhāḥ parīkṣya ca punaḥpunaḥ ..33..
3.65.d:
तथा च रक्षाधिकृताननुरूपेण योजयेत् ॥
विभवेन द्विज श्रेष्ठाः परीक्ष्य च पुनःपुनः ॥33॥
3.65.m: And thus he should appoint those placed in charge of protection with suitable / wealth, O foremost of twice-born, and after examining them repeatedly.

3.65.s:
rājā karmaniyuktānāṃ strīṇāṃ preṣyajanasya ca ..
pratyahaṃ kalpayed vṛttiṃ sthānakarmānurūpataḥ ..34..
3.65.d:
राजा कर्मनियुक्तानां स्त्रीणां प्रेष्यजनस्य च ॥
प्रत्यहं कल्पयेद् वृत्तिं स्थानकर्मानुरूपतः ॥34॥
3.65.m: The king should assign a daily livelihood to women appointed to labor / and to servant-folk, in accordance with their position and work.

3.65.s:
āyadvārāṃśca nocchindyādviśeṣadvārakānapi ..
samyagbaliśca gṛhṇīyānmālākāropamāṃ nṛpaḥ .. 35 ..
3.65.d:
आयद्वारांश्च नोच्छिन्द्याद्विशेषद्वारकानपि ॥
सम्यग्बलिश्च गृह्णीयान्मालाकारोपमां नृपः ॥ 35 ॥
3.65.m: He should not cut off avenues of revenue, nor even the special avenues; / and the king should collect tribute properly, in the manner of a garland-maker.

3.65.s:
krayavikrayamadhvānaṃ bhaktañcāsaparivyayam ..
yogakṣemañca samprekṣya vaṇijo dāpayetkaram .. 36 ..
3.65.d:
क्रयविक्रयमध्वानं भक्तञ्चासपरिव्ययम् ॥

ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
राज्ञो धर्मस्त्वया प्रोक्तो व्यवहारान्ववेक्षणम् ॥
तदस्माकं त्वमाचक्ष्व त्वं हि सर्वविदुच्यसे ॥1॥
हंस उवाच ॥
आसीत्कृतयुगे पूर्वे प्रजाधर्मनिबन्धनः ॥
ततस्त्रेतायुगे तेषां धर्मो नाशमुपागमत् ॥ 2 ॥
धर्मे नष्टे मनुष्याणां व्यवहारः प्रवर्तितः ॥
द्रष्टा च व्यवहाराणां राजा दण्डधरः कृतः ॥ ॥3 ॥

व्यवहारान्नृपः पश्येद्विद्वद्भिर्ब्राह्मणैः सह ॥

3.65.m:
There is no toll on a fraction of a kārṣāpaṇa, nor on an artisan’s trade, nor on an infant, nor on a messenger, / nor on what is obtained by alms, on what remains of property plundered, nor on a Vedic scholar, an ascetic, or a sacrifice.
3.324
The sages said:
The duty of a king has been proclaimed by you as the investigation of legal disputes; / expound that to us, for you are declared to be all-knowing.
Haṃsa said:
In the past, in the Kṛta age, the subject-folk were bound by dharma; / then, in the Tretā age, their dharma went to ruin.
When dharma was destroyed, legal procedure was set in motion among men, / and the king, holding the rod of punishment, was made the overseer of legal disputes.
Families, guilds, corporations, and the appointed royal officer: / these are overseers of legal disputes, each higher [in authority] than the preceding.
The king should investigate legal disputes together with learned brahmins, / in accordance with the treatises on dharma, free from desire and aversion.
Born of good family, steadfast in dharma, endowed with purity, possessed of learning, / who are impartial toward enemy and friend—such should the king make court assessors.

अपश्यता कार्यवशाद्व्यवहारान्नृपेण तु ॥ ॥
सभ्यैः सह नियोक्तव्यो ब्राह्मणः सर्वधर्मवित् ॥ 7 ॥
क्षत्त्रियस्त्वथ वा वैश्यो न तु शूद्रः कदाचन ॥
यस्य राज्ञस्तु विषये शूद्रो धर्मविवेचकः ॥ 8 ॥
तस्य सीदति तद्राष्ट्रं दुर्भिक्षव्याधितस्करैः ॥
विवादाद् द्विगुणं दंडं कूटकृत्साक्षिणस्तथा ॥ 9 ॥
द्विगुणं च तथा सभ्या रागद्वेषव्यवस्थिताः ॥
दुर्मृष्टव्यवहारेण राज्ञा वित्तं यदर्जितम् ॥ 3.324.10 ॥
त्रिंशद्गुणं तु दातव्यं ब्राह्मणेष्वथ वांभसि ॥
स्मृत्याचारव्यपेतेन मार्गेणाधर्षितः परैः ॥ 11 ॥
आवेदयति चेद्राज्ञे व्यवहारपदं हि तत् ॥
प्रत्यर्थिनस्तथा कुर्यादाह्वानं पृथिवीपतिः ॥ 12 ॥
अनागच्छञ्जितो राज्ञा विनेयः पुरुषो भृशम्॥
नदीसन्तारकारण्यदुर्देशोपप्लवादिषु ॥13॥
3.65.m:
If unable to examine legal disputes due to pressing business, the king / should appoint a brahmin who knows all dharma together with the court assessors.
Or else a kṣatriya or a vaiśya, but never a śūdra. / In whichever king’s realm a śūdra is an adjudicator of dharma,
his realm perishes from famine, disease, and thieves. / The maker of false witnesses [shall receive] twice the fine of the dispute;
and likewise twice [the fine for] court assessors settled in passion and hatred. / Whatever wealth has been obtained by the king through unjust legal procedure,
thirty times that must be given to brahmins or cast into water. / Oppressed by others through a path departing from traditional law and custom,
if he reports to the king, that is indeed an occasion of legal dispute. / The lord of the earth should likewise summon the defendant.
One who does not come is defeated and must be severely punished by the king; / [except when hindered] in crossing a river, in a forest, in a bad country, in calamities, and the like,

3.65.d:
नागस्थो न स दंड्यः स्यान्नासौ राज्ञोपराध्यति ॥
निवेष्टुकामो रोगार्तो यियक्षुर्व्यसने स्थितः॥14॥
अभियुक्तस्तथान्येन राजकार्यरतस्तथा ॥
गवां प्रचारे गोपालाः सम्पत्काले कृषीवलाः ॥15 ॥
शिल्पिनश्चैव तत्कालं चायुधेयाश्च विग्रहे ॥
अपास्तव्यवहाराश्च दूतदानो मुखी व्रते ॥ 16 ॥
विषमस्थश्च नासाध्या नचैनांश्चाह्वयेन्नृपः ॥
प्रत्यर्थिनोऽग्रतो लेख्यं यथावेदितमर्थिनः ॥ 17 ॥
समामासतदर्धाहर्ज्ञातिनामादिचिह्नितम् ॥
श्रुतार्थस्योत्तरं लेख्यं पूर्वावेदकसंनिधौ ॥18॥
ततोर्थी लेखयेत्सद्यः प्रतिज्ञातार्थसाधनम् ॥
चतुर्धा तच्च कथितं मुनिभिस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥19 ॥
लिखितं साक्षिणो भुक्तिश्चतुर्थी वैदिकी क्रिया ॥
सारस्तु व्यवहाराणां प्रतिष्ठा समुदाहृता ॥3.324.20 ॥
3.65.m:
nor when standing in an elephant-force—he should not be punished, nor does he offend against the king; / nor one desirous of marrying, afflicted with illness, wishing to sacrifice, or involved in a calamity;
likewise one accused by another, or engaged in royal business, / cowherds while pasturing cattle, farmers at harvest time,
and craftsmen at that time, and warriors in battle, / and those who have cast off litigation, an envoy giving [a message], one intent on a vow,
nor should a person situated in distress be approached, nor should the king summon them. / The statement of the plaintiff, as reported, is to be written down before the defendant,
marked with the year, the month, its fortnight, the day, the caste, the name, and so forth; / and the reply of the one who heard the matter is to be written down in the presence of the original complainant.
Then the claimant should immediately have the proof of the asserted matter recorded; / and that has been declared fourfold by the sages who see reality:
document, witnesses, possession, and the fourth is a Vedic procedure [by ordeal]. / The essence is declared to be the firm foundation of legal disputes.

3.65.d:
सर्वस्माद्धीयते चार्थादिति धर्मविदो विदुः ॥
बलोपधिनिवृत्ताम्̐स्तु व्यवहारान्निवर्त्तयेत् ॥29॥
स्त्रीनक्तमन्तरागारबहुशत्रुकृताम्̐स्तथा ॥
रोगार्त्तभीतव्यसनिबालशिष्यकृतानि तु ॥ 3.324.30 ॥
अकृतानि विजानीयात्तथा दासकृतानि तु॥
गुरोर्वाक्येन शिष्यस्य पितृवाक्यात्सुतस्य च ॥ 31 ॥
दासस्य स्वामिवाक्येन व्यवहारस्तु सिद्ध्यति ॥
स्त्रीकृतान्यप्रमाणानि कार्याण्याहुरनापदि ॥32 ॥
विशेषतो धनक्षेत्रे दायादधनविक्रमाः ॥
एतान्येव प्रमाणानि भर्ता यद्यनुमन्यते ॥ 33 ॥
पुरः पत्युरभावेन राजा वा पितृपुत्रयोः ॥
बाल आषोडशावर्षात्पौगण्डश्चाभिशस्यते ॥ 34 ॥
परतो व्यवहारज्ञः स्वतन्त्रः पितरं विना ॥
अप्राप्तव्यवहारस्य स्वातंत्र्यं मातुरुच्यते ॥ 35 ॥
अस्वतन्त्रकृतान्याहुरप्रमाणानि पंडिताः ॥
नानियुक्तेन वक्तव्यं व्यवहारे कथंचन ॥ 36 ॥
3.65.m:
he is deprived of the entire claim: so know those who know dharma. / But legal proceedings brought about by force or fraud, one should annul;
likewise those carried out by women, at night, in an inner room, or by many enemies; / but those executed by the diseased, the frightened, the distressed, children, and pupils
one should know as not executed, and likewise those carried out by slaves. / But by the word of a teacher for a pupil, and by the word of a father for a son,
and by the word of a master for a slave, a legal transaction is established. / Transactions executed by women are said to be invalid in the absence of an emergency,
especially regarding money and land, or the sale of an heir's property; / yet these very acts are valid if the husband approves.
In the absence of a husband, in the presence of the king, or of a father and son, [a decision is made]. / A child is up to sixteen years of age, and a youth is designated as paugaṇḍa.
Thereafter, he is competent in legal affairs and independent, except with respect to his father; / for one who has not attained legal majority, independence belongs to the mother.
The wise state that transactions executed by dependent persons are invalid. / Nothing whatsoever should be spoken in a legal dispute by one who is not appointed.

3.65.d:
अनियुक्तवचो दण्ड्यो राजा रुक्मस्य कृष्णलम् ॥
नियुक्तो न नियुक्तो वा विद्या वाक्यमुदाहरन् ॥ 37 ॥
सर्वस्वरहितः कार्यो लेखकोऽनृतलेखकः ॥
लेखकस्य च सभ्यानां साक्षिणां यश्च दूषकः ॥38॥
अनाहूतस्य चाह्वाने आहूतस्य च मोक्षणे ॥
अजितोऽस्मीति मन्वानो ब्रूयात्तं तु पराजितम् ॥ 39 ॥
राजा तान्विनयेद्विप्रान्दंडेन द्विगुणेन च ॥
सभा वा न प्रवेष्टव्या वक्तव्यं वासमंजसम् ॥ 3.324.40 ॥
अब्रुवन्विब्रुवन्वापि नरो भवति किल्बिषी ॥
पादो धर्मस्य कर्तारं पादः साक्षिणमेव च ॥ 41 ॥
पादः सभासदः सर्वान्पादो राजानमृच्छति ॥
राजा भवत्यनेनास्तु निन्दार्हो यत्र निन्द्यते ॥ 42 ॥
एनो गच्छति कर्तारं मुच्यन्ते च सभासदः ॥
छलं निरस्य भूतेन व्यवहारान्नयेन्नृपः॥43॥
3.65.m:
The king should fine one who speaks without being appointed a kṛṣṇala of gold; / whether appointed or not appointed, one who knows the law should utter the relevant statement.
A scribe who writes false statements must be stripped of all his property, / as also one who corrupts the scribe, the court assessors, or the witnesses.
In summoning one who was not summoned, and in releasing one who was summoned, / or if one, thinking 'I am not defeated,' should speak, [the king should declare] him defeated.
The king should punish those [guilty] brahmins with a double fine. / Either the assembly should not be entered, or fair speech must be spoken;
speaking nothing, or speaking falsely, a man becomes sinful. / One-fourth of the sin of adharma falls upon the perpetrator, one-fourth upon the witness,
one-fourth falls upon all the assessors, and one-fourth reaches the king. / But the king becomes guiltless where one deserving censure is censured;
the sin goes to the perpetrator, and the assessors are released. / Setting aside trickery, the king should conduct legal proceedings according to the truth.

3.65.s:
bhūtamapyanupanyastaṃ vyavahāreṇa hīyate..
sapaṇaścedvivādaḥ syātaddhanaṃ dāpayennaraḥ..

āgamena viśuddhena bhogo yāti pramāṇatām ..

bhuktireva viśuddhā syātprāptānāṃ pitṛtaḥ kramāt..3..

pareṇa bhujyamānāyā dhanasya daśavārṣakī .. 5 ..
3.65.d:
भूतमप्यनुपन्यस्तं व्यवहारेण हीयते॥
सपणश्चेद्विवादः स्यातद्धनं दापयेन्नरः॥
दण्डं च स्वपणं चैव धनिके धनमेव च॥44॥
न सा सभा यत्र न संति वृद्धा न ते वृद्धा ये न वदंति धर्मम्॥
न तद्धर्मं यत्र न सत्यमस्ति न तत्सत्यं यच्छलेनानुविद्धम्॥45॥
3.225
हंस उवाच ॥
संभोगो दृश्यते यत्र न दृश्येतागमः क्वचित् ॥
आगमः कारणं तत्र न भोगस्तत्र कारणम्॥1॥
आगमेन विशुद्धेन भोगो याति प्रमाणताम् ॥
अविशुद्धागमो भोगः प्रामाण्यं नैव गच्छति ॥ 2 ॥
आहंतैवाभियुक्तः सन्नर्थानामुद्धरेत्पदम् ॥
भुक्तिरेव विशुद्धा स्यात्प्राप्तानां पितृतः क्रमात्॥3॥
अन्वाहितः ॥॥। हेले विस्पष्टयाचितम् ॥
अप्रत्यक्षं च यद्भुक्तं न चेद्भोगेन जीर्यते॥4॥
पश्यतोऽब्रुवतो भूमेर्हानिर्विंशतिवार्षिकी ॥
परेण भुज्यमानाया धनस्य दशवार्षकी ॥ 5 ॥
3.65.m:
Even a fact, if not presented, is lost in a lawsuit. / If the dispute involves a stake, the man must be made to pay that sum: / the fine, his own stake, and to the creditor his money.
That is not an assembly where there are no elders; they are not elders who do not speak dharma; / that is not dharma where there is no truth; that is not truth which is tainted with deceit.
3.325 / Haṃsa said: / Where possession is observed, but title is nowhere seen, / title is the determining factor there, not possession.
Through a pure title, possession becomes authoritative; / possession with an impure title never attains authoritativeness.
Only the claimant being accused should establish the basis of the property; / but possession alone is pure in the case of [property] obtained successively from ancestors.
A bailment […], what is clearly begged for, / and what is enjoyed out of sight, does not lapse by possession.
For land being enjoyed by another while [the owner] looks on and says nothing, the loss of title occurs after twenty years; / for movable property, after ten years.

3.65.s:
tribhireva tu yadbhuktaṃ puruṣaistu yathāvidhi ..
lekhyābhāvepi taṃ tatra caturthaḥ samavāpnuyāt .. 6 ..

āgamopi balī naiva bhuktistatrāpi yatra na..7..
