3.65.d:
त्रिभिरेव तु यद्भुक्तं पुरुषैस्तु यथाविधि ॥
लेख्याभावेपि तं तत्र चतुर्थः समवाप्नुयात् ॥ 6 ॥
आगमोप्यधिको भुक्तेर्विनापूर्वक्रमागतात् ॥
आगमोपि बली नैव भुक्तिस्तत्रापि यत्र न॥7॥
आध्याभिहस्ता स भृशं विनेया दण्डेन विप्रा द्विगुणेन राज्ञा ॥
लोके न दुष्टः स तु कंटकः स्यात्पापात्मनां मूर्धनि तिष्ठतीति॥॥॥
3.65.m:
What has been enjoyed according to rule by three generations of men, / the fourth generation should obtain in that case even in the absence of a written document.
Title is superior to possession, except in the case of what has descended from ancestors; / yet even title has no strength where there is no possession at all.
Seized by force, she/it must be severely punished by the king with a double fine, O brahmins; / let that thorn not remain corrupt in the world, standing on the head of evildoers […]

3.66.s:
3.326
haṃsa uvāca ..
pauruṣaścaiva divyaśca nirṇayo dvividhaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
dvividhaḥ pauruṣastatra likhitaṃ sākṣiṇastathā .. 1 ..
3.66.d:
3.326
हंस उवाच ॥
पौरुषश्चैव दिव्यश्च निर्णयो द्विविधः स्मृतः ॥
द्विविधः पौरुषस्तत्र लिखितं साक्षिणस्तथा ॥ 1 ॥
3.66.m: 3.326 / Haṃsa said: / Judgment is declared to be twofold: human and divine. / Among these, the human is twofold: written documents and witnesses.

3.66.s:
trividhaṃ likhitaṃ tatra tasya vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam ..
rājasākṣikamekaṃ tu dvitīyaṃ tu sa sākṣikam ..2 ..
3.66.d:
त्रिविधं लिखितं तत्र तस्य वक्ष्यामि लक्षणम् ॥
राजसाक्षिकमेकं तु द्वितीयं तु स साक्षिकम् ॥2 ॥
3.66.m: A written document is of three kinds in that regard; I will state its characteristics: / one attested by the king, the second attested by witnesses,

3.66.s:
svahastalikhitaṃ nāma tṛtīyaṃ parikīrtitam..
niyuktakāryasya kṛtaṃ rājādhikaraṇetaram .. 3 ..
3.66.d:
स्वहस्तलिखितं नाम तृतीयं परिकीर्तितम्॥
नियुक्तकार्यस्य कृतं राजाधिकरणेतरम् ॥ 3 ॥
3.66.m: and the third is proclaimed as written in one's own hand. / That executed by an appointed official in the royal court of justice

3.66.s:
tadadhyakṣyeṇa martyaiśca svahasta paricihnitam ..
tallekhyaṃ kathitaṃ loke rājasākṣikamityuta..
yatra kvacana vipreṃdrā likhitaṃ yena kenacita ..
cihnitaṃ yatsvahastena sākṣibhiśca guṇānvitaiḥ ..5..
3.66.d:
तदध्यक्ष्येण मर्त्यैश्च स्वहस्त परिचिह्नितम् ॥
तल्लेख्यं कथितं लोके राजसाक्षिकमित्युत॥
यत्र क्वचन विप्रेंद्रा लिखितं येन केनचित ॥
चिह्नितं यत्स्वहस्तेन साक्षिभिश्च गुणान्वितैः ॥5॥
3.66.m: and signed with their own hands by its supervisor and by men, / that document is called in the world 'attested by the king.' / Wherever, O foremost of brahmins, a document is written by anyone whatsoever, / and signed with their own hand and by qualified witnesses,

3.66.s:
dvābhyāmūrdhvaṃ tu tajjñeyaṃ likhitañca sasākṣikam ..
sākṣī svahastalikhite bhavedvāpi na vā bhavet..6..
3.66.d:
द्वाभ्यामूर्ध्वं तु तज्ज्ञेयं लिखितञ्च ससाक्षिकम् ॥
साक्षी स्वहस्तलिखिते भवेद्वापि न वा भवेत्॥6॥
3.66.m: above two in number, that is to be known as a document attested by witnesses. / There may or may not be a witness in a document written in one's own hand;

3.66.s:
vināpi sākṣibhistasya prāmāṇyamupapadyate ..
svahastalikhitaṃ patraṃ balātkāreṇa kāritam..7..
3.66.d:
विनापि साक्षिभिस्तस्य प्रामाण्यमुपपद्यते ॥
स्वहस्तलिखितं पत्रं बलात्कारेण कारितम्॥7॥
3.66.m: its validity is established even without witnesses. / A document written in one's own hand that was caused to be made by force,

3.66.s:
hastapramāṇaṃ sarvairvā tathopadhikṛtaṃ dvijāḥ ..
mattonmattakṛtaṃ lekhyamasvatantrakṛtaṃ ca yat..8..
3.66.d:
हस्तप्रमाणं सर्वैर्वा तथोपधिकृतं द्विजाः ॥
मत्तोन्मत्तकृतं लेख्यमस्वतन्त्रकृतं च यत्॥8॥
3.66.m: or written by all under duress, or made through fraud, O twice-born, / or a document made by an intoxicated or insane person, or made by a dependent, [is invalid].

3.66.s:
lekhyaṃ vinā nāsti siddhiḥ sthāvarasya tu karhicit ..
bhuktistatra pramāṇaṃ vā bhavettripuruṣāgatā..9..
3.66.d:
लेख्यं विना नास्ति सिद्धिः स्थावरस्य तु कर्हिचित् ॥
भुक्तिस्तत्र प्रमाणं वा भवेत्त्रिपुरुषागता॥9॥
3.66.m: Without a written document, there is never legal establishment of immovable property, / or possession that has descended through three generations can be the proof in that case.

3.66.s:
hastena dvipadaṃ deyaṃ sāmnā dadyāccatuṣpadam ..
sthāvarāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ siddhirlekhye pratiṣṭhitā ..3.326.10..
3.66.d:
हस्तेन द्विपदं देयं साम्ना दद्याच्चतुष्पदम् ॥
स्थावराणां च सर्वेषां सिद्धिर्लेख्ये प्रतिष्ठिता ॥3.326.10॥
3.66.m: Two-footed beings should be given by the hand; four-footed beings one should give with soothing words; / and the legal establishment of all immovable properties rests upon a written document.

3.66.s:
deśācārādviruddhaṃ yadvyaktāvavadhilakṣaṇam ..
tatpramāṇaṃ smṛtaṃ lekhyaṃ viluptadhanamakṣayam .. 11 ..
3.66.d:
देशाचाराद्विरुद्धं यद्व्यक्ताववधिलक्षणम् ॥
तत्प्रमाणं स्मृतं लेख्यं विलुप्तधनमक्षयम् ॥ 11 ॥
3.66.m: A document that is not contrary to local custom, has clear specifications of boundaries, / and whose property is intact and imperishable, is declared to be authoritative.

3.66.s:
prākprasādāḥ pradīyante paścādvāpi na pārthivāḥ ..
devadvijātivitteṣu na syātsvāmī nṛpaḥ kvacit .. 12 ..
3.66.d:
प्राक्प्रसादाः प्रदीयन्ते पश्चाद्वापि न पार्थिवाः ॥
देवद्विजातिवित्तेषु न स्यात्स्वामी नृपः क्वचित् ॥ 12 ॥
3.66.m: Grants given earlier or later are not [revocable by] kings. / A king should never be the owner over the property of gods and twice-born people.

3.66.s:
samūhārthe na bhogo'sti lekhyaṃ tatrāpahārakam ..
ubhayorapi tatra syādbhuktaṃ yena sa vai prabhuḥ .. 13 ..
3.66.d:
समूहार्थे न भोगोऽस्ति लेख्यं तत्रापहारकम् ॥
उभयोरपि तत्र स्याद्भुक्तं येन स वै प्रभुः ॥ 13 ॥
3.66.m: There is no [mere] possession in the case of corporate property; a document is that which sets it aside there. / Where it belongs to both, he indeed is the master by whom it has been enjoyed.

3.66.s:
cirantanamavijñātaṃ bhuktaṃ bhogānna cālayet ..
ekārha likhite tatsyātsambhogo yasya tasya tu .. 14 ..
3.66.d:
चिरन्तनमविज्ञातं भुक्तं भोगान्न चालयेत् ॥
एकार्ह लिखिते तत्स्यात्सम्भोगो यस्य तस्य तु ॥ 14 ॥
3.66.m: One should not disturb from possession what is ancient, of unknown [origin], and possessed. / If it is written for one [person], that belongs to him who enjoys it.

3.66.s:
arvākkālikalabdhaṃ tu lekhyenaiva viśodhayet ..
mudrāśuddhaṃ kriyāśuddhaṃ pāraṃparyānumoditam ..15 ..
3.66.d:
अर्वाक्कालिकलब्धं तु लेख्येनैव विशोधयेत् ॥
मुद्राशुद्धं क्रियाशुद्धं पारंपर्यानुमोदितम् ॥15 ॥
3.66.m: What is acquired in recent times, however, one must substantiate solely by a document / that is clear of seal-defects, verified by formal transaction, and approved through tradition,

3.66.s:
adūṣitaṃ ca spaṣṭaṃ ca siddhimāpnoti nānyathā ..
svaveśātkīrtayedrājā ātmānaṃ tadanantaram..16..
3.66.d:
अदूषितं च स्पष्टं च सिद्धिमाप्नोति नान्यथा ॥
स्ववेशात्कीर्तयेद्राजा आत्मानं तदनन्तरम्॥16॥
3.66.m: and unvitiated and clear; [only thus] does it attain validity, not otherwise. / The king should then proclaim himself according to his own status.

3.66.s:
dāyādeyapramāṇaṃ ca sahasīmāparicchadaiḥ ..
tatastu lekhayettatra dānacchedopavarṇanam .. 17 ..
3.66.d:
दायादेयप्रमाणं च सहसीमापरिच्छदैः ॥
ततस्तु लेखयेत्तत्र दानच्छेदोपवर्णनम् ॥ 17 ॥
3.66.m: And [he should record] the extent of the inheritance to be given, together with its boundaries and appurtenances. / Then he should cause a description of the donation and alienation to be written down therein.

3.66.s:
tallekhyaṃ siddhimāpnoti mudritaṃ rājamudrayā ..
matāntare tu lekhyasya śrāvaṇācchravaṇe tathā .. 18 ..
3.66.d:
तल्लेख्यं सिद्धिमाप्नोति मुद्रितं राजमुद्रया ॥
मतान्तरे तु लेख्यस्य श्रावणाच्छ्रवणे तथा ॥ 18 ॥
3.66.m: That document attains validity when stamped with the royal seal. / But in another tradition, upon read-out and hearing of the document,

3.66.s:
naiva siddhirvinirdiṣṭā bhāvanānyā na cedbhavet ..
svahastalikhitaṃ patraṃ nihnuke tu vibhāvayet .. 19 ..
3.66.d:
नैव सिद्धिर्विनिर्दिष्टा भावनान्या न चेद्भवेत् ॥
स्वहस्तलिखितं पत्रं निह्नुके तु विभावयेत् ॥ 19 ॥
3.66.m: validity is not declared at all, unless there is another proof. / If a deed written in one's own hand is denied, he should prove it

3.66.s:
varṇaiśca tatkṛtaiścihnaiḥ prāpyaireva ca yuktibhiḥ ..
yatrarṇalekhako vāpi sākṣī vāpi mṛto bhavet .. 3.326.20 ..
3.66.d:
वर्णैश्च तत्कृतैश्चिह्नैः प्राप्यैरेव च युक्तिभिः ॥
यत्रर्णलेखको वापि साक्षी वापि मृतो भवेत् ॥ 3.326.20 ॥
3.66.m: by the letters, by the signs made by him, and by accessible arguments. / Where the writer of the debt or the witness has died,

3.66.s:
likhitānte praviṣṭe tu dhanī lekhyaṃ tu pāṭayet ..
asamagre praviṣṭe tu lekhye dūragate tathā .. .. 21..
3.66.d:
लिखितान्ते प्रविष्टे तु धनी लेख्यं तु पाटयेत् ॥
असमग्रे प्रविष्टे तु लेख्ये दूरगते तथा ॥ ॥ 21॥
3.66.m: when it has entered at the end of what was written, the creditor should tear the document. / But when [the debt] is partially repaid, or when the document has gone far away,

3.66.s:
dhanikasya dhanī dadyāllikhitaṃ svamathāparam ..
daivadopaniviṣṭaṃ tu lekhyaṃ lekhyaṃ tu kārayet .. 22 ..
3.66.d:
धनिकस्य धनी दद्याल्लिखितं स्वमथापरम् ॥
दैवदोपनिविष्टं तु लेख्यं लेख्यं तु कारयेत् ॥ 22 ॥
3.66.m: the creditor should give another document of his own to the creditor. / But if a document is spoiled by accident, he should cause [another] document to be made,

3.66.s:
anyamevādhamarṇāstu lekhyaṃ yatsmaryate yadi ..
samudre tu yadā lekhye mṛtāḥ sarve tu tatsthitāḥ .. 23 ..
3.66.d:
अन्यमेवाधमर्णास्तु लेख्यं यत्स्मर्यते यदि ॥
समुद्रे तु यदा लेख्ये मृताः सर्वे तु तत्स्थिताः ॥ 23 ॥
3.66.m: or indeed another [written by] the debtors, if the document is remembered. / But when on a sealed document all those residing on it have died,

3.66.s:
likhitaṃ tatpramāṇaṃ tu mṛteṣvapi hi sākṣiṣu ..
sopadhyaṃ yadbhavellekhyaṃ divyādyaistatprasādhayet .. 24 ..
3.66.d:
लिखितं तत्प्रमाणं तु मृतेष्वपि हि साक्षिषु ॥
सोपध्यं यद्भवेल्लेख्यं दिव्याद्यैस्तत्प्रसाधयेत् ॥ 24 ॥
3.66.m: that writing is an authority even though the witnesses are dead. / A document that is fraudulent one should prove through divine [ordeals] and the like.

3.66.s:
balātkārabalairlekhyaiḥ satyaścecchachrāvaṇādbhavet ..
jñāpitenāpyasiddhiḥ syātsiddhistasmādyathā smṛtā ..
paitāmahānāṃ rikthānāṃ prabhuḥ pautro'pi gāyate .. 25 ..
3.66.d:
बलात्कारबलैर्लेख्यैः सत्यश्चेच्छछ्रावणाद्भवेत् ॥
ज्ञापितेनाप्यसिद्धिः स्यात्सिद्धिस्तस्माद्यथा स्मृता ॥
पैतामहानां रिक्थानां प्रभुः पौत्रोऽपि गायते ॥ 25 ॥
3.66.m: If [a claim made] through documents [executed] by forces of duress would become true from a hearing, / even when made known there would be invalidity; therefore, validity is as declared. / Even a grandson is declared the master of ancestral estates.

3.66.s:
ye kūṭakārā vasudhādhipena bhṛśaṃ vineyāstridaśepsunā vai ..
te kaṇṭakāḥ sarvajanasya viprāsteṣāṃ niṣeddhā nṛpatirbhavedvai .. 26 ..
3.327
.. haṃsa uvāca .. ..
ekādaśavidhaḥ sākṣī śāstradṛṣṭo manīṣibhiḥ ..
kṛtaḥ pañcavidhastatra ṣaḍvidho'kṛta ucyate .. 1 ..
likhitaḥ smāritaścaiva yadṛcchābhijña eva ca ..
gūḍhaścottarasākṣī ca kṛtaḥ pañcavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 2 ..
grāmaśca prāḍvivākaśca rājā ca vyavahāriṇām ..
kāryeṣvabhyantaro yaḥ syādarthinā prahitaḥ sadā .. 3 ..
kulaṃ kulavivādeṣu ṣaḍvidhastvakṛtaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
dvayorvivadatorarthe dvayoḥ satsu ca sākṣiṣu ..4..
pūrvapakṣo bhavedyasya bhaveyustasya sākṣiṇaḥ ..
ādhāryaḥ pūrvapakṣasya yasminnarthavaśādbhavet .. 5 ..
vivāde sākṣiṇastatra praṣṭavyāḥ prativādinaḥ ..
na pareṇa samuddiṣṭamupeyātsākṣiṇaṃ prati .. 6 ..
3.66.d:
ये कूटकारा वसुधाधिपेन भृशं विनेयास्त्रिदशेप्सुना वै ॥
ते कण्टकाः सर्वजनस्य विप्रास्तेषां निषेद्धा नृपतिर्भवेद्वै ॥ 26 ॥
3.327
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
एकादशविधः साक्षी शास्त्रदृष्टो मनीषिभिः ॥
कृतः पञ्चविधस्तत्र षड्विधोऽकृत उच्यते ॥ 1 ॥
लिखितः स्मारितश्चैव यदृच्छाभिज्ञ एव च ॥
गूढश्चोत्तरसाक्षी च कृतः पञ्चविधः स्मृतः ॥ 2 ॥
ग्रामश्च प्राड्विवाकश्च राजा च व्यवहारिणाम् ॥
कार्येष्वभ्यन्तरो यः स्यादर्थिना प्रहितः सदा ॥ 3 ॥
कुलं कुलविवादेषु षड्विधस्त्वकृतः स्मृतः ॥
द्वयोर्विवदतोरर्थे द्वयोः सत्सु च साक्षिषु ॥4॥
पूर्वपक्षो भवेद्यस्य भवेयुस्तस्य साक्षिणः ॥
आधार्यः पूर्वपक्षस्य यस्मिन्नर्थवशाद्भवेत् ॥ 5 ॥
विवादे साक्षिणस्तत्र प्रष्टव्याः प्रतिवादिनः ॥
न परेण समुद्दिष्टमुपेयात्साक्षिणं प्रति ॥ 6 ॥
3.66.m:
Those who are forgers must be severely punished by the lord of the earth who desires [to attain] the gods. / They are thorns to all people, O brahmins; the king should indeed be their restrainer.
Haṃsa said: / A witness has been seen in the treatise by the wise as elevenfold: / made, of five kinds there; unmade is said to be of six kinds.
Written, reminded, one who happened by, / secret, and a secondary witness: [these] are considered the fivefold made [witness].
The village, the chief judge, and the king of litigants; / he who is an insider in transactions, always sent by the plaintiff;
the family in family disputes: [these] are considered the sixfold unmade. / When two [parties] dispute over property and there are witnesses on both sides,
whose prima facie claim it is, his should be the witnesses. / In whatever [matter] the basis of the prima facie claim would be held on account of the object,
in that dispute the witnesses of the defendant must be questioned. / One should not approach a witness cited by another [party];

3.66.s:
bhedayettu na vānyonyaṃ hīyatyevaṃ samācaret ..
sākṣidviṣṭo yadi preyādgacchedvāpi digantaram .. 7 ..
taccobhayoḥ pramāṇaṃ tu pramāṇe hyantarā kriyā ..
anirdiṣṭastu sākṣitve svayamevaitya yo vadet .. 8 ..
sūcītyuktaḥ sa sākṣī tu na sa sākṣitvamarhati ..
na sākṣī nṛpatiḥ kāryo na kārukakuśīlavau .. 9 ..
na śrotriyo na liṅgastho na sarvebhyo vinirgataḥ ..
na vyādhito na vaktavyo na dasyurna vikarmakṛt .. 3.327.10 ..
na vṛddho na śiśurnaiko nāndho na vikalendriyaḥ ..
nārto na matto nonmatto na kṣuttṛṣṇopapīḍitaḥ .. 11 ..
na śramārto na kāmārto na kruddho nāpi taskaraḥ ..
nārthasambandhinorāpto na hāyanavicāriṇaḥ .. 12 ..
na dṛṣṭadoṣāḥ kartavyā na vyādhyārtā na dūṣitāḥ ..
strīṇāṃ sākṣyaṃ striyaḥ kuryurdvijānāṃ sadṛśā dvijāḥ .. 13 ..
3.66.d:
भेदयेत्तु न वान्योन्यं हीयत्येवं समाचरेत् ॥
साक्षिद्विष्टो यदि प्रेयाद्गच्छेद्वापि दिगन्तरम् ॥ 7 ॥
तच्चोभयोः प्रमाणं तु प्रमाणे ह्यन्तरा क्रिया ॥
अनिर्दिष्टस्तु साक्षित्वे स्वयमेवैत्य यो वदेत् ॥ 8 ॥
सूचीत्युक्तः स साक्षी तु न स साक्षित्वमर्हति ॥
न साक्षी नृपतिः कार्यो न कारुककुशीलवौ ॥ 9 ॥
न श्रोत्रियो न लिङ्गस्थो न सर्वेभ्यो विनिर्गतः ॥
न व्याधितो न वक्तव्यो न दस्युर्न विकर्मकृत् ॥ 3.327.10 ॥
न वृद्धो न शिशुर्नैको नान्धो न विकलेन्द्रियः ॥
नार्तो न मत्तो नोन्मत्तो न क्षुत्तृष्णोपपीडितः ॥ 11 ॥
न श्रमार्तो न कामार्तो न क्रुद्धो नापि तस्करः ॥
नार्थसम्बन्धिनोराप्तो न हायनविचारिणः ॥ 12 ॥
न दृष्टदोषाः कर्तव्या न व्याध्यार्ता न दूषिताः ॥
स्त्रीणां साक्ष्यं स्त्रियः कुर्युर्द्विजानां सदृशा द्विजाः ॥ 13 ॥
3.66.m:
nor should he cause division between them; he who does so is defeated. / If a witness who has been specified should die or go to another region,
that is proof for both; for when there is proof, intermediate procedure [applies]. / One who, not indicated as a witness, comes and speaks on his own accord,
is called an informer-witness; he does not deserve witness status. / A king must not be made a witness, nor an artisan or an actor,
nor a Vedic scholar, nor an ascetic, nor one detached from all, / nor one who is diseased, nor one under reproach, nor a robber, nor an evildoer,
nor an old man, nor a child, nor a single person, nor a blind man, nor one with impaired senses, / nor one in distress, nor an intoxicated man, nor an insane man, nor one afflicted by hunger and thirst,
nor one afflicted by fatigue, nor one afflicted by lust, nor an angry man, nor a thief, / nor a relative of the two parties, nor those who travel for a year,
nor those whose faults are seen, nor those afflicted by disease, nor the corrupted. / Women should testify for women, like twice-born for twice-born,

3.66.s:
śūdrāśca sādhuśūdrāṇāṃ martyānāṃ martyayonayaḥ ..
anubhāvī tu yaḥ kaścitkuryātsākṣyaṃ vivādinām .. 14 ..
antarveśmanyaraṇye vā śarīrasya tathātyaye ..
striyo'pi sambhave kāryā bālena sthavireṇa vā .. 15 ..
śiṣyeṇa bandhunā vāpi dāsena bhṛtakena vā ..
bālavṛddhāturāṇāṃ tu sākṣye tu vadatāṃ mṛṣā ..16..
jānīyādadhivācamutsiktamanasāṃ tathā ..
gṛhiṇaḥ putriṇo maulāḥ śūdrā viṭkṣatrayonayaḥ ..17..
atyuktāḥ sākṣyamarhanti naye kūṭadhanāpadi ..
āptāḥ sarveṣu varṇeṣu kāryāḥ kāryeṣu sākṣiṇaḥ ..18..
bahutve parigṛhṇīyātsākṣitve vetanādhipam ..
sameṣu tvaguṇotkṛṣṭaṃ guṇitve vai dvijottamān ..19..
samakṣadarśanātsākṣyaṃ śravaṇāccaiva sidhyati ..
tatra satyaṃ bruvansākṣī dharmārthābhyāṃ na hīyate .. 3.327.20 ..
3.66.d:
शूद्राश्च साधुशूद्राणां मर्त्यानां मर्त्ययोनयः ॥
अनुभावी तु यः कश्चित्कुर्यात्साक्ष्यं विवादिनाम् ॥ 14 ॥
अन्तर्वेश्मन्यरण्ये वा शरीरस्य तथात्यये ॥
स्त्रियोऽपि सम्भवे कार्या बालेन स्थविरेण वा ॥ 15 ॥
शिष्येण बन्धुना वापि दासेन भृतकेन वा ॥
बालवृद्धातुराणां तु साक्ष्ये तु वदतां मृषा ॥16॥
जानीयादधिवाचमुत्सिक्तमनसां तथा ॥
गृहिणः पुत्रिणो मौलाः शूद्रा विट्क्षत्रयोनयः ॥17॥
अत्युक्ताः साक्ष्यमर्हन्ति नये कूटधनापदि ॥
आप्ताः सर्वेषु वर्णेषु कार्याः कार्येषु साक्षिणः ॥18॥
बहुत्वे परिगृह्णीयात्साक्षित्वे वेतनाधिपम् ॥
समेषु त्वगुणोत्कृष्टं गुणित्वे वै द्विजोत्तमान् ॥19॥
समक्षदर्शनात्साक्ष्यं श्रवणाच्चैव सिध्यति ॥
तत्र सत्यं ब्रुवन्साक्षी धर्मार्थाभ्यां न हीयते ॥ 3.327.20 ॥
3.66.m:
and śūdras for worthy śūdras, mortals of mortal birth [for mortals]. / But anyone who is a direct observer may bear witness for disputants
inside a house, in a forest, or at the loss of life. / Even women must be employed if available, or a child or an elder,
or a disciple, or a kinsman, or a slave, or a hired servant. / But when children, elders, and sick persons speak falsely in testimony,
one should know their speech as excessive, as also that of arrogant minds. / Householders who have sons, indigenous, śūdras, born of vaiśya and kṣatriya [lineage],
are eligible for testimony when spoken to, in cases of forgery or financial calamity. / Trustworthy persons among all castes should be made witnesses in legal cases.
In a multiplicity [of witnesses], one should accept the master of the fee; / in equality, the one superior in virtue; and in virtue, the foremost twice-born.
Witness testimony succeeds from seeing with one's own eyes and from hearing. / There, speaking the truth, a witness does not fall away from dharma and wealth.

3.66.s:
sākṣī dṛṣṭaśrutādanyadvibruvannarakaṃ vrajet ..
pṛṣṭāni baddho'pi vadedyathā dṛṣṭaṃ yathāśrutam .. 21 ..
eko lubdhastvasākṣī syādbahavo'pi na vā kvacit ..
svabhāvenaiva yadbrūyustadgrāhyaṃ vyāvahārikam .. 22..
na jātu sākṣiṇaḥ prāptānarthipratyarthisannidhau ..
prāḍvivāko niyuṃjīta vidhinānena sāntvayan .. 23 ..
yattayoranayorvettha kārye'smiṃśceṣṭite'pi vā ..
tad brūta sarvaṃ satyena yuṣmākaṃ hyatra sākṣitam .. 24 ..
devabrāhmaṇasānnidhye sākṣyaṃ pṛcchettato dvijāḥ ..
udaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukho vā pūrvāhṇe vai śuciḥ śucīn .. 25 ..
brūhīti brāhmaṇaṃ pṛcchetsatyaṃ brūhīti pārthivam ..
gobījakāñcanairvaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ sarvaistu pātakaiḥ .. 26 ..
3.66.d:
साक्षी दृष्टश्रुतादन्यद्विब्रुवन्नरकं व्रजेत् ॥
पृष्टानि बद्धोऽपि वदेद्यथा दृष्टं यथाश्रुतम् ॥ 21 ॥
एको लुब्धस्त्वसाक्षी स्याद्बहवोऽपि न वा क्वचित् ॥
स्वभावेनैव यद्ब्रूयुस्तद्ग्राह्यं व्यावहारिकम् ॥ 22॥
न जातु साक्षिणः प्राप्तानर्थिप्रत्यर्थिसन्निधौ ॥
प्राड्विवाको नियुंजीत विधिनानेन सान्त्वयन् ॥ 23 ॥
यत्तयोरनयोर्वेत्थ कार्येऽस्मिंश्चेष्टितेऽपि वा ॥
तद् ब्रूत सर्वं सत्येन युष्माकं ह्यत्र साक्षितम् ॥ 24 ॥
देवब्राह्मणसान्निध्ये साक्ष्यं पृच्छेत्ततो द्विजाः ॥
उदङ्मुखः प्राङ्मुखो वा पूर्वाह्णे वै शुचिः शुचीन् ॥ 25 ॥
ब्रूहीति ब्राह्मणं पृच्छेत्सत्यं ब्रूहीति पार्थिवम् ॥
गोबीजकाञ्चनैर्वैश्यं शूद्रं सर्वैस्तु पातकैः ॥ 26 ॥
3.66.m:
A witness declaring otherwise than what was seen and heard goes to hell. / Even if bound, when questioned he should speak just as seen and just as heard.
A single greedy man cannot be a witness, nor many [such] anywhere. / What they speak by their very nature, that is acceptable in a legal proceeding.
Never should the chief judge appoint witnesses who have arrived in the presence of the plaintiff and defendant / [without] comforting them by this rule:
'Whatever you know concerning these two in this matter or in their action, / speak all that with truth, for your status here is that of a witness.'
Then, in the presence of deities and brahmins, O twice-born, / facing north or facing east, in the morning, clean himself, he should question the clean [witnesses]:
He should ask a brahmin, saying 'Speak'; a kṣatriya, saying 'Speak the truth'; / a vaiśya, by cows, seeds, and gold; and a śūdra, by all sins.

3.66.s:
brahmaṇe ca smṛtā lokā ye ca strībāla ghātinaḥ ..
mitradruhaḥ kṛtaghnasya tatte syurbruvatāṃ mṛṣā .. 27 ..
3.66.d:
ब्रह्मणे च स्मृता लोका ये च स्त्रीबाल घातिनः ॥
मित्रद्रुहः कृतघ्नस्य तत्ते स्युर्ब्रुवतां मृषा ॥ 27 ॥
3.66.m: The worlds taught for a slayer of a brahmin, and those of the killers of women and children, / of the betrayer of friends, and of the ungrateful—let those be yours if you speak falsely.

3.66.s:
janmaprabhṛti yatkiñcitkiñcitpuṇyaṃ tvayā kṛtam ..
tatsarvaṃ tasya jānīhi yaṃ parājayase mṛṣā .. 28 ..
3.66.d:
जन्मप्रभृति यत्किञ्चित्किञ्चित्पुण्यं त्वया कृतम् ॥
तत्सर्वं तस्य जानीहि यं पराजयसे मृषा ॥ 28 ॥
3.66.m: Whatever merit has been acquired by you since your birth, / know that all of it belongs to him whom you falsely cause to lose.

3.66.s:
nagno muṇḍaḥ kapālī ca bhikṣārthī kṣutpipāsitaḥ ..
andhaḥ śatrugṛhaṃ gacchedyatsākṣyamanṛtaṃ vadet .. 29 ..
3.66.d:
नग्नो मुण्डः कपाली च भिक्षार्थी क्षुत्पिपासितः ॥
अन्धः शत्रुगृहं गच्छेद्यत्साक्ष्यमनृतं वदेत् ॥ 29 ॥
3.66.m: Naked, shaven-headed, carrying a skull-bowl, begging for alms, tormented by hunger and thirst, / and blind, he shall go to the house of his enemy—[the one] who speaks false testimony.

3.66.s:
etāṃstu doṣānvīkṣya tvaṃ sarvānanṛtabhāṣaṇāt ..
yathāśrutaṃ yathādṛṣṭaṃ sarvamevāñjasā vada .. 3.327.30 ..
3.66.d:
एतांस्तु दोषान्वीक्ष्य त्वं सर्वाननृतभाषणात् ॥
यथाश्रुतं यथादृष्टं सर्वमेवाञ्जसा वद ॥ 3.327.30 ॥
3.66.m: Recognising all these faults that arise from speaking falsehood, / speak directly everything exactly as heard, exactly as seen.

3.66.s:
satyaṃ sākṣyaṃ bruvansākṣī lokānprāpnotyanuttamān ..
iha vānuttamāṃ kīrtiṃ vāgyeṣāṃ brahmapūjitā .. 31 ..
3.66.d:
सत्यं साक्ष्यं ब्रुवन्साक्षी लोकान्प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमान् ॥
इह वानुत्तमां कीर्तिं वाग्येषां ब्रह्मपूजिता ॥ 31 ॥
3.66.m: Speaking true testimony, a witness attains the highest worlds, / or unsurpassed fame here, whose speech is honoured by Brahmā.

3.66.s:
manyante vai pāpakṛto na kaścitpaśyatīti naḥ ..
tāṃśca devāḥ prapaśyanti svasyaivāntarapūruṣaḥ .. 32 ...
ādityacandrāvanalānilau ca dyaurbhūmirāpo hṛdayaṃ yamaśca ..
ahaśca rātriśca ubhe ca sandhye dharmaśca jānāti narasya vṛttam .. 33 ..
3.328
haṃsa uvāca ..
pauruṣo nirṇayaḥ prokto divyaṃ vakṣyāmyataḥ param ..
asākṣikeṣu tvartheṣu mitho vivadamānayoḥ .. 1 ..
rājadrohābhiśāpeṣu sāhaseṣu tathaiva ca ..
vivāde tattvataḥ satyaṃ śapathenāpi lambhayet .. 2 ..
maharṣibhiśca devaiśca kāryārthaṃ śapathāḥ kṛtāḥ ..
vasiṣṭho'datta śapathaṃ samaye javane nṛpe .. 3 ..
na mṛṣā śapathaṃ kuryātsvalpe'pyarthe naro budhaḥ ..
vṛthā hi śapathaṃ kurvanpretya ceha ca naśyati .. 4 ..
sthāvareṣu tu divyāni varjanīyāni pārthivaiḥ ..
likhitena tathā bhuktyā teṣāṃ bhavati sādhanam .. 5 ..
3.66.d:
मन्यन्ते वै पापकृतो न कश्चित्पश्यतीति नः ॥
तांश्च देवाः प्रपश्यन्ति स्वस्यैवान्तरपूरुषः ॥ 32 ॥।
आदित्यचन्द्रावनलानिलौ च द्यौर्भूमिरापो हृदयं यमश्च ॥
अहश्च रात्रिश्च उभे च सन्ध्ये धर्मश्च जानाति नरस्य वृत्तम् ॥ 33 ॥
3.328
हंस उवाच ॥
पौरुषो निर्णयः प्रोक्तो दिव्यं वक्ष्याम्यतः परम् ॥
असाक्षिकेषु त्वर्थेषु मिथो विवदमानयोः ॥ 1 ॥
राजद्रोहाभिशापेषु साहसेषु तथैव च ॥
विवादे तत्त्वतः सत्यं शपथेनापि लम्भयेत् ॥ 2 ॥
महर्षिभिश्च देवैश्च कार्यार्थं शपथाः कृताः ॥
वसिष्ठोऽदत्त शपथं समये जवने नृपे ॥ 3 ॥
न मृषा शपथं कुर्यात्स्वल्पेऽप्यर्थे नरो बुधः ॥
वृथा हि शपथं कुर्वन्प्रेत्य चेह च नश्यति ॥ 4 ॥
स्थावरेषु तु दिव्यानि वर्जनीयानि पार्थिवैः ॥
लिखितेन तथा भुक्त्या तेषां भवति साधनम् ॥ 5 ॥
3.66.m:
Evildoers indeed think: "No one sees us." / Yet the gods see them, and so does one's own inner person. / The sun and moon, fire and wind, heaven, earth, water, the heart and Yama, / day and night, both twilights, and Dharma know the conduct of a mortal.
The Haṃsa said: / The human determination [of disputes] has been declared; hereafter I shall declare divine ordeal, / when two people are mutually disputing in matters that have no witnesses.
In treason against the king, false accusations, and likewise in violent crimes, / in a lawsuit one should obtain the truth in its reality even by means of an oath.
Oaths have been made by the great sages and by the gods for the sake of matters [of law]; / Vasiṣṭha gave an oath when King Javana entered into a covenant.
A wise man should not take a false oath, even in a very small matter; / for one who takes a futile oath perishes in the next world and in this one.
In the case of immoveable property, ordeals are to be avoided by kings; / their proof is established by written documents as well as by possession.

3.66.s:
kośaṃ dhaṭaṃ viṣaṃ cāgnimudakaṃ taptamāṣakam ..
phālaṃ ca taṇḍulaṃ caiva divyānyaṣṭau vidurbudhāḥ .. 6 ..
kośavarjantu divyāni saśiraskāni dāpayet ..
aśiraskaḥ smṛtaḥ kośaḥ kālāntaravibhāvanāta .. 7 ..
aśiraskāni divyāni rājñā kaṇṭakaśodhanaiḥ ..
rājñā sarvāṇi deyāni svayaṃ ca parimārgiṇā .. .. 8 ..
lobhānmohādbhayādvāpi bhidyante sākṣiṇaḥ paraiḥ ..
ajñānādbālabhāvācca bhede dharmo vyavasthitaḥ .. 9 ..
sarvadravyeṣu kanakaṃ mūlyaṃ tu parikalpayet ..
māṣakeṇa suvarṇasya ..........kālyamasukhe dvijam .. 3.328.10 ..
satyaṃ vadāmīti śapennānyatkiñcana pārthiva ..
śastramādāya vaktavyaṃ kṣattriyeṇa tathaiva ca .. 11 ..
dhenuṃ saṃspṛśatā satyaṃ vācyaṃ vaiśyena vai dvijāḥ ..
śūdraḥ kurvīta śapathaṃ tathā sarvaistu pātakaiḥ .. 12 ..
3.66.d:
कोशं धटं विषं चाग्निमुदकं तप्तमाषकम् ॥
फालं च तण्डुलं चैव दिव्यान्यष्टौ विदुर्बुधाः ॥ 6 ॥
कोशवर्जन्तु दिव्यानि सशिरस्कानि दापयेत् ॥
अशिरस्कः स्मृतः कोशः कालान्तरविभावनात ॥ 7 ॥
अशिरस्कानि दिव्यानि राज्ञा कण्टकशोधनैः ॥
राज्ञा सर्वाणि देयानि स्वयं च परिमार्गिणा ॥ ॥ 8 ॥
लोभान्मोहाद्भयाद्वापि भिद्यन्ते साक्षिणः परैः ॥
अज्ञानाद्बालभावाच्च भेदे धर्मो व्यवस्थितः ॥ 9 ॥
सर्वद्रव्येषु कनकं मूल्यं तु परिकल्पयेत् ॥
माषकेण सुवर्णस्य ॥॥॥॥॥काल्यमसुखे द्विजम् ॥ 3.328.10 ॥
सत्यं वदामीति शपेन्नान्यत्किञ्चन पार्थिव ॥
शस्त्रमादाय वक्तव्यं क्षत्त्रियेण तथैव च ॥ 11 ॥
धेनुं संस्पृशता सत्यं वाच्यं वैश्येन वै द्विजाः ॥
शूद्रः कुर्वीत शपथं तथा सर्वैस्तु पातकैः ॥ 12 ॥
3.66.m:
Sacred water, the balance, poison, fire, water, the heated bean-weight, / the ploughshare, and sacred grain—the wise know these as the eight ordeals.
Except for the sacred water, one should administer ordeals accompanied by a penalty; / the sacred water is taught as being free from penalty, due to its manifestation over a period of time.
Ordeals free from penalty are to be administered by the king when extirpating criminals; / they are all to be administered by the king himself when he investigates [a matter].
Witnesses are divided by opponents out of greed, delusion, or fear, / or out of ignorance or childishness; when there is divergence, dharma remains settled.
Among all commodities one should estimate the value in gold; / by a māṣaka of gold […] a twice-born in difficulty.
O king, he should swear: "I speak the truth," and nothing else; / likewise, [an oath] should be spoken by a kṣatriya after taking up a weapon.
The truth is to be spoken by a vaiśya while touching a cow, O twice-born; / a śūdra should take an oath through all grave sins.

3.66.s:
kṛṣṇalena suvarṇasya tilavṛddhyā tu śāpayet ..
śūdrānna śāpayedrājā kadācidapi vai dvijāḥ ..13 ..
vipravarjaṃ tathā kośaṃ varṇināṃ dāpayennṛpaḥ ..
suvarṇamāṣakādūrdhvamarvāgaṣṭabhya eva ca .. 14 ..
vipravarjaṃ tu vipro'pi varṇināṃ pūrasaṃyutam ..
kośasthāne tu śapathaṃ kārayedavidhārayan .. 15 ..
ataḥ paraṃ tu divyānāṃ kuryādanyatamaṃ naraḥ ..
yathā tathā mahīpālaḥ śṛṇudhvaṃ gadato mama .. 16 ..
na śīte tu dhaṭaṃ deyamuṣṇakāle hutāśanam ..
varṇināṃ na tathā phālaṃ taṇḍulaṃ mukharogiṇām .. 17 ..
śvāsakāsārditānāṃ ca brāhmaṇānāṃ ca no viṣam ..
taptamāṣakamarhanti sarve varṇā niratyayam .. 18 ..
na vyādhimarakākrānte deśe kośaṃ tu pātayet ..
mantrairasvaradivyāni sañcayantīha mānavāḥ ..19..
pratimantravidaḥ stambhanānāṃ vināśane ..
niyuñjīta narendropi nibhṛtāṃ dhanavatsalām .. 3.328.20 ..
3.66.d:
कृष्णलेन सुवर्णस्य तिलवृद्ध्या तु शापयेत् ॥
शूद्रान्न शापयेद्राजा कदाचिदपि वै द्विजाः ॥13 ॥
विप्रवर्जं तथा कोशं वर्णिनां दापयेन्नृपः ॥
सुवर्णमाषकादूर्ध्वमर्वागष्टभ्य एव च ॥ 14 ॥
विप्रवर्जं तु विप्रोऽपि वर्णिनां पूरसंयुतम् ॥
कोशस्थाने तु शपथं कारयेदविधारयन् ॥ 15 ॥
अतः परं तु दिव्यानां कुर्यादन्यतमं नरः ॥
यथा तथा महीपालः शृणुध्वं गदतो मम ॥ 16 ॥
न शीते तु धटं देयमुष्णकाले हुताशनम् ॥
वर्णिनां न तथा फालं तण्डुलं मुखरोगिणाम् ॥ 17 ॥
श्वासकासार्दितानां च ब्राह्मणानां च नो विषम् ॥
तप्तमाषकमर्हन्ति सर्वे वर्णा निरत्ययम् ॥ 18 ॥
न व्याधिमरकाक्रान्ते देशे कोशं तु पातयेत् ॥
मन्त्रैरस्वरदिव्यानि सञ्चयन्तीह मानवाः ॥19॥
प्रतिमन्त्रविदः स्तम्भनानां विनाशने ॥
नियुञ्जीत नरेन्द्रोपि निभृतां धनवत्सलाम् ॥ 3.328.20 ॥
3.66.m:
One should administer an oath by a kṛṣṇala of gold, with an increase of a sesame grain; / the king, O twice-born, should never administer an oath to śūdras [by gold].
Except for the brahmin, the king should administer the ordeal of sacred water to members of the classes, / [in cases valued] above a golden māṣaka and up to eight [māṣakas].
Except for a brahmin, even a brahmin [judge], without hesitating, / should have an oath taken in place of sacred water for members of the classes, accompanied by the city [officials].
Beyond this, a man should perform one of the ordeals; / O ruler of the earth, listen as I speak how [it is done].
The balance is not to be administered in cold weather, nor fire in the hot season; / likewise, the ploughshare is not for members of the classes, nor sacred grain for those suffering from mouth disease.
Poison is not [to be given] to those afflicted with asthma and cough, nor to brahmins; / all classes are eligible for the heated bean-weight without transgression.
One should not administer sacred water in a country overwhelmed by disease and plague; / men here hinder divine ordeals by means of mantras.
A ruler of men should also employ those who know counter-mantras to destroy paralyzing spells— / [officials who are] discreet and fond of wealth.

3.66.s:
divyānāṃ stambhakaṃ jñātvā pāpānnityaṃ mahīpatiḥ ..
vivāsayetsvakādrāṣṭrātte hi lokasya kaṇṭakāḥ .. 21 ..
teṣāmanveṣaṇe yatnaṃ rājā nityaṃ samācaret ..
te hi pāpasamācārāstaskarebhyopi taskarāḥ .. 22 ..
dṛgdṛṣṭidoṣātsvalpepi divyeṣu viniyojayet ..
mahatsvapi na cārtheṣu dharmajñāndharmavatsalān .. 23 ..
jñātvā dharmiṣṭhatāṃ rājā puruṣassa vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
svalpe vāpyatha vāsvalpe śapathe tānniyojayet .. 24 ..
na mithyāvacanaṃ yeṣāṃ janmaprabhṛti vidyate ..
śraddadhyātpārthivasteṣāṃ vacane dharmadarśinām ..25 ..
atyantopahatāḥ pāpā nāstikā bhinnasetavaḥ ..
divyānyarhaṃti sarvāṇi svalpadoṣā api dvijāḥ .. 26 ..
ādau bhūmiṃ parīkṣeta dhaṭasyārthe vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
indrasthāne sabhāyāṃ vā digbhāge pūrvadakṣiṇe .. 27 ..
3.66.d:
दिव्यानां स्तम्भकं ज्ञात्वा पापान्नित्यं महीपतिः ॥
विवासयेत्स्वकाद्राष्ट्रात्ते हि लोकस्य कण्टकाः ॥ 21 ॥
तेषामन्वेषणे यत्नं राजा नित्यं समाचरेत् ॥
ते हि पापसमाचारास्तस्करेभ्योपि तस्कराः ॥ 22 ॥
दृग्दृष्टिदोषात्स्वल्पेपि दिव्येषु विनियोजयेत् ॥
महत्स्वपि न चार्थेषु धर्मज्ञान्धर्मवत्सलान् ॥ 23 ॥
ज्ञात्वा धर्मिष्ठतां राजा पुरुषस्स विचक्षणः ॥
स्वल्पे वाप्यथ वास्वल्पे शपथे तान्नियोजयेत् ॥ 24 ॥
न मिथ्यावचनं येषां जन्मप्रभृति विद्यते ॥
श्रद्दध्यात्पार्थिवस्तेषां वचने धर्मदर्शिनाम् ॥25 ॥
अत्यन्तोपहताः पापा नास्तिका भिन्नसेतवः ॥
दिव्यान्यर्हंति सर्वाणि स्वल्पदोषा अपि द्विजाः ॥ 26 ॥
आदौ भूमिं परीक्षेत धटस्यार्थे विचक्षणः ॥
इन्द्रस्थाने सभायां वा दिग्भागे पूर्वदक्षिणे ॥ 27 ॥
3.66.m:
Knowing someone to be a delayer of ordeals, the lord of the earth should always banish / the wicked from his own realm, for they are thorns to the people.
The king should always make an effort in searching for them; / for those who behave wickedly are thieves greater than thieves.
He may assign [people] to ordeals even for a small [matter] due to an eye or vision defect; / but he should not assign those who know dharma and are fond of dharma, even in great matters.
Knowing someone to be most righteous, that discerning king / should assign them to an oath, whether the matter is small or not small.
Those in whom no false word has been found since birth— / the king should place faith in the word of those who perceive dharma.
Those who are utterly corrupted, wicked, atheists, and breakers of moral bounds, / even if their offense is small, O twice-born, are fit for all ordeals.
First, the discerning [king] should inspect the ground for the purpose of the balance, / at the place of Indra or in the court of justice, or in the south-eastern direction.

3.66.s:
dhaṭaṃ niveśayettatra susamāyāṃ tathā bhuvi ..
yajñiyasya tu vṛkṣasya kartavyaṃ maṇḍapadvayam .. 28 ..
maṇḍapasya pramāṇaṃ tu saptahastaṃ prakīrtitam ..
dvau hastau nikhanetkāṣṭhaṃ dṛśyaṃ syāddhastapañcakam .. 29 ..
antarañca tayoḥ kāryaṃ tathā hastacatuṣṭayam ..
maṇḍapopari kāṣṭhaṃ ca dṛḍhaṃ kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ .. 3.328.30 ..
caturhastaṃ tulākāṣṭhaṃ tvavraṇaṃ kārayetsthiram ..
khadirārjunavṛkṣāṇāṃ śiṃśipāsālajaṃ tathā .. 31 ..
tulākāṣṭhaṃ tu kartavyaṃ tathā vai śikyakadvayam ..
prāṅmukho niścalaḥ kāryaḥ śucau deśe dhaṭastathā .. 32 ..
vaṇiksuvarṇakārau ca kulālaḥ kāṃsyakārakaḥ ..
tulādhare dhaṭaḥ kāryo ripau mitre tathā samaḥ .. 33 ..
3.66.d:
धटं निवेशयेत्तत्र सुसमायां तथा भुवि ॥
यज्ञियस्य तु वृक्षस्य कर्तव्यं मण्डपद्वयम् ॥ 28 ॥
मण्डपस्य प्रमाणं तु सप्तहस्तं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
द्वौ हस्तौ निखनेत्काष्ठं दृश्यं स्याद्धस्तपञ्चकम् ॥ 29 ॥
अन्तरञ्च तयोः कार्यं तथा हस्तचतुष्टयम् ॥
मण्डपोपरि काष्ठं च दृढं कुर्याद्विचक्षणः ॥ 3.328.30 ॥
चतुर्हस्तं तुलाकाष्ठं त्वव्रणं कारयेत्स्थिरम् ॥
खदिरार्जुनवृक्षाणां शिंशिपासालजं तथा ॥ 31 ॥
तुलाकाष्ठं तु कर्तव्यं तथा वै शिक्यकद्वयम् ॥
प्राङ्मुखो निश्चलः कार्यः शुचौ देशे धटस्तथा ॥ 32 ॥
वणिक्सुवर्णकारौ च कुलालः कांस्यकारकः ॥
तुलाधरे धटः कार्यो रिपौ मित्रे तथा समः ॥ 33 ॥
3.66.m:
There he should set up the balance on very level ground; / two pavilions are to be made of a sacrificial tree.
The measure of the pavilion is declared to be seven cubits; / one should dig in two cubits of the wooden post, and five cubits should be visible.
The space between the two should be made four cubits; / and above the pavilion the discerning [builder] should make the crossbeam strong.
One should make the beam of the balance four cubits long, free from defects, and stable, / made of khadira, arjuna, śiṃśipā, or sāla trees.
The beam of the balance is to be made thus, and likewise two suspension baskets; / the balance is to be made facing east, motionless, in a pure place.
The balance-holder should be a merchant, goldsmith, potter, or coppersmith; / the balance must be made impartial towards enemy and friend.

3.66.s:
śrāvayetprāḍvivākopi tulādhāraṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
brahmaghno ye smṛtā lokā ye ca strībālaghātinām .. 34 ..
3.66.d:
श्रावयेत्प्राड्विवाकोपि तुलाधारं विचक्षणः ॥
ब्रह्मघ्नो ये स्मृता लोका ये च स्त्रीबालघातिनाम् ॥ 34 ॥
3.66.m: The discerning chief judge should recite to the balance-holder: / "The worlds that are taught for a brahmin-slayer, and those of the slayers of women and children—

3.66.s:
tulādharasya te lokāstulāṃ dhārayato mṛṣā ..
ekasmim̐stolayecchikye snātaṃ sūpoṣitaṃ naram .. 35 ..
3.66.d:
तुलाधरस्य ते लोकास्तुलां धारयतो मृषा ॥
एकस्मिम्̐स्तोलयेच्छिक्ये स्नातं सूपोषितं नरम् ॥ 35 ॥
3.66.m: those worlds belong to the balance-holder who holds the balance falsely." / In one suspension basket he should weigh the man who has bathed and fasted well.

3.66.s:
dvitīye mṛttikāṃ śubhrāṃ gaurīṃ tu tulayedbudhaḥ ..
iṣṭakābhasmapāṣāṇakapālāsthīni varjayet .. 36 ..
3.66.d:
द्वितीये मृत्तिकां शुभ्रां गौरीं तु तुलयेद्बुधः ॥
इष्टकाभस्मपाषाणकपालास्थीनि वर्जयेत् ॥ 36 ॥
3.66.m: In the second [pan], the wise man should weigh pure, pale earth; / he should avoid bricks, ashes, stones, potsherds, and bones.

3.66.s:
tulayitvā tataḥ pūrvaṃ tasmāttamavatārayet ..
mūrdhni patraṃ tatastasya nyastapatraṃ niveśayet .. 37 ..
3.66.d:
तुलयित्वा ततः पूर्वं तस्मात्तमवतारयेत् ॥
मूर्ध्नि पत्रं ततस्तस्य न्यस्तपत्रं निवेशयेत् ॥ 37 ॥
3.66.m: Having weighed him first, he should then take him down from it; / then he should place upon his head a document written with a text.

3.66.s:
mantraścāyaṃ purā proktaḥ svayameva svayambhuvā ..
brahmaṇastvaṃ sutā devi tulānāmnīti kathyase .. 38 ..
3.66.d:
मन्त्रश्चायं पुरा प्रोक्तः स्वयमेव स्वयम्भुवा ॥
ब्रह्मणस्त्वं सुता देवि तुलानाम्नीति कथ्यसे ॥ 38 ॥
3.66.m: And this mantra was uttered of old by the Self-born himself: / "O goddess, you are the daughter of Brahmā, and you are called by the name Tulā (Balance).

3.66.s:
tukāro gauravo nityaṃ lakāro laghuni smṛtaḥ ..
gurulāghavasaṃyogāttulā tena nigadyase .. 39 ..
3.66.d:
तुकारो गौरवो नित्यं लकारो लघुनि स्मृतः ॥
गुरुलाघवसंयोगात्तुला तेन निगद्यसे ॥ 39 ॥
3.66.m: The syllable 'tu' is always remembered for heaviness (gaurava), and the syllable 'la' for lightness (laghu); / because of the union of heaviness and lightness, therefore you are called Tulā.

3.66.s:
saṃśayānmocaya svainaṃ cābhiśastaṃ naraṃ śubhe ..
bhūya āropayettaṃ tu naraṃ tasyāṃ sapatrakam .. 3.328.40 ..
3.66.d:
संशयान्मोचय स्वैनं चाभिशस्तं नरं शुभे ॥
भूय आरोपयेत्तं तु नरं तस्यां सपत्रकम् ॥ 3.328.40 ॥
3.66.m: O auspicious one, release this accused man from doubt!" / He should then mount the man onto it once more, along with the document.

3.66.s:
tulito yadi vardheta śubho bhavati dharmataḥ ..
hīyamāne na śuddhaḥ syāditi dharmavido viduḥ .. 41 ..
3.66.d:
तुलितो यदि वर्धेत शुभो भवति धर्मतः ॥
हीयमाने न शुद्धः स्यादिति धर्मविदो विदुः ॥ 41 ॥
3.66.m: If, when weighed, he increases [in weight], he is auspicious according to dharma; / if he decreases, he cannot be pure: so know the knowers of dharma.

3.66.s:
śikyacchede tulābhaṅge punarāropayennaram ..
tathā niḥsaṃśayaṃ jñānaṃ bhavatīti viniścayaḥ .. 42 ..
3.66.d:
शिक्यच्छेदे तुलाभङ्गे पुनरारोपयेन्नरम् ॥
तथा निःसंशयं ज्ञानं भवतीति विनिश्चयः ॥ 42 ॥
3.66.m: If a sling breaks or the balance snaps, he should mount the man again; / thus infallible knowledge arises: such is the decision.

3.66.s:
agnervidhiṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇudhvaṃ gadato mama ..
saptamaṇḍalakānkuryāddevabrāhmaṇasannidhau .. 43 ..
3.66.d:
अग्नेर्विधिं प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुध्वं गदतो मम ॥
सप्तमण्डलकान्कुर्याद्देवब्राह्मणसन्निधौ ॥ 43 ॥
3.66.m: I shall explain the rite of fire; listen as I speak! / He should make seven small circles in the presence of the gods and brahmins.

3.66.s:
pratyakṣaṃ kārayeddivyaṃ rājño vādhikṛtasya vā ..
brāhmaṇānāṃ śrutavatāṃ prakṛtīnāṃ tathaiva ca .. 44 ..
3.66.d:
प्रत्यक्षं कारयेद्दिव्यं राज्ञो वाधिकृतस्य वा ॥
ब्राह्मणानां श्रुतवतां प्रकृतीनां तथैव च ॥ 44 ॥
3.66.m: He should cause the ordeal to take place before the eyes of the king or his appointed officer, / of learned brahmins, and likewise of the subjects.

3.66.s:
paścime maṇḍale tiṣṭhetprāṅmukhaḥ prāñjaliḥ śuciḥ ..
caraturasre yathā asminkṛtvā caiva samau karau .. 45 ..
3.66.d:
पश्चिमे मण्डले तिष्ठेत्प्राङ्मुखः प्राञ्जलिः शुचिः ॥
चरतुरस्रे यथा अस्मिन्कृत्वा चैव समौ करौ ॥ 45 ॥
3.66.m: In the western circle, pure, facing east, with joined hands, / having made both hands flat in this square [manner],

3.66.s:
lakṣayeyuḥ kṣatādīni hastayostasya kāriṇaḥ ..
saptāśvatthasya patrāṇi badhnīyuḥ karayostataḥ .. 46 ..
3.66.d:
लक्षयेयुः क्षतादीनि हस्तयोस्तस्य कारिणः ॥
सप्ताश्वत्थस्य पत्राणि बध्नीयुः करयोस्ततः ॥ 46 ॥
3.66.m: the officiants should examine the wounds and so forth on the hands of that person; / then they should bind seven leaves of the holy fig tree onto his hands,

3.66.s:
navena sitasūtreṇa kārpāsena dvijottamāḥ ..
tatastu susamaṃ kṛtvā aṅgulaṃ tvekamāyasam ..47..
3.66.d:
नवेन सितसूत्रेण कार्पासेन द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
ततस्तु सुसमं कृत्वा अङ्गुलं त्वेकमायसम् ॥47॥
3.66.m: with a new, white cotton thread, O best of the twice-born. / Then, having made completely even an iron ball of one aṅgula,

3.66.s:
piṇḍaṃ hutāśasantaptaṃ pañcāśatpalikaṃ dṛḍham ..
ādau pūjāṃ hutāśasya kārayedvasudhādhipaḥ ..48..
3.66.d:
पिण्डं हुताशसन्तप्तं पञ्चाशत्पलिकं दृढम् ॥
आदौ पूजां हुताशस्य कारयेद्वसुधाधिपः ॥48॥
3.66.m: weighing fifty palas, solid, heated in fire— / first the lord of the earth should cause worship of the fire to be performed

3.66.s:
raktacandanadhūmābhyāṃ raktapuṣpaistathaiva ca ..
abhiśastasya mantraṃ ca badhnīyāttasya mūrdhani .. 49 ..
3.66.d:
रक्तचन्दनधूमाभ्यां रक्तपुष्पैस्तथैव च ॥
अभिशस्तस्य मन्त्रं च बध्नीयात्तस्य मूर्धनि ॥ 49 ॥
3.66.m: with red sandalwood and incense, and likewise with red flowers; / and he should bind the mantra upon the head of the accused,

3.66.s:
mantreṇānena saṃyuktaṃ brāhmaṇābhihitena tu ..
tvamagne vedāścatvārastvaṃ ca yajñeṣu hūyase..3.328.50..
3.66.d:
मन्त्रेणानेन संयुक्तं ब्राह्मणाभिहितेन तु ॥
त्वमग्ने वेदाश्चत्वारस्त्वं च यज्ञेषु हूयसे॥3.328.50॥
3.66.m: equipped with this mantra spoken by a brahmin: / "O Fire, you are the four Vedas, and you are offered in sacrifices;

3.66.s:
tvaṃ mukhaṃ sarvadevānāṃ tvaṃ mukhaṃ brahmavādinām..
jaṭharasthopi bhūtānāṃ tvaṃ ca vetsi śubhāśubham..
pāpeṣu darśayātmānamarciṣmānbhava pāvaka .. 51 ..
3.66.d:
त्वं मुखं सर्वदेवानां त्वं मुखं ब्रह्मवादिनाम्॥
जठरस्थोपि भूतानां त्वं च वेत्सि शुभाशुभम्॥
पापेषु दर्शयात्मानमर्चिष्मान्भव पावक ॥ 51 ॥
3.66.m: you are the mouth of all the gods, you are the mouth of the knowers of the Veda; / dwelling even in the belly of living beings, you know good and bad! / Show yourself against sins; be radiant, O Purifier!

3.66.s:
atha vā śuddhabhāveṣu śīto bhava mahābala ..
tatobhiśastaḥ śanakairmaṇḍalāni parikramet .. 52 ..
3.66.d:
अथ वा शुद्धभावेषु शीतो भव महाबल ॥
ततोभिशस्तः शनकैर्मण्डलानि परिक्रमेत् ॥ 52 ॥
3.66.m: Or, towards those of pure disposition, be cool, O mighty one!" / Then the accused should slowly pace through the circles.

3.66.s:
parikramya śanairjahyāllohapiṇḍaṃ tathā kṣitau ..
vimuktahastaṃ taṃ paścātkārayedvrīhimarddanam .. 53 ..
3.66.d:
परिक्रम्य शनैर्जह्याल्लोहपिण्डं तथा क्षितौ ॥
विमुक्तहस्तं तं पश्चात्कारयेद्व्रीहिमर्द्दनम् ॥ 53 ॥
3.66.m: Having paced through, he should likewise drop the iron ball slowly onto the ground; / once his hands are free, he should afterwards cause him to rub unhusked rice.

3.66.s:
nirvikārau karau dṛṣṭvā śuddho bhavati dharmataḥ ..
bhayādvā pātayedyastu dagdho vā na vibhāvyate ..54..
3.66.d:
निर्विकारौ करौ दृष्ट्वा शुद्धो भवति धर्मतः ॥
भयाद्वा पातयेद्यस्तु दग्धो वा न विभाव्यते ॥54॥
3.66.m: Seeing both hands unblemished, he becomes pure according to dharma; / but if he drops it out of fear, or if it is not clearly discerned whether he is burned,

3.66.s:
punastu cāharellohaṃ vidhireṣa prakīrtitaḥ ..
toyasyātha pravakṣyāmi vidhiṃ dharmyaṃ sanātanam .. 55 ..
3.66.d:
पुनस्तु चाहरेल्लोहं विधिरेष प्रकीर्तितः ॥
तोयस्याथ प्रवक्ष्यामि विधिं धर्म्यं सनातनम् ॥ 55 ॥
3.66.m: he should take the iron again: such is the rule proclaimed. / Now I shall declare the righteous, eternal rule of water.

3.66.s:
śaivālanakramatsyādyairvarjite sthāvare jale ..
dharmasthūṇā tatra kāryā puruṣaṃ dharmavatsalam .. 56 ..
3.66.d:
शैवालनक्रमत्स्याद्यैर्वर्जिते स्थावरे जले ॥
धर्मस्थूणा तत्र कार्या पुरुषं धर्मवत्सलम् ॥ 56 ॥
3.66.m: In still water devoid of moss, crocodiles, fish, and the like, / a post of dharma is to be set up there. A man fond of dharma

3.66.s:
nābhidaghnodakasthasya gṛhītvottaṃ samāviśet ..
madhyamenātha dhanuṣā madhyasthaḥ puruṣo'paraḥ .. 57..
3.66.d:
नाभिदघ्नोदकस्थस्य गृहीत्वोत्तं समाविशेत् ॥
मध्यमेनाथ धनुषा मध्यस्थः पुरुषोऽपरः ॥ 57॥
3.66.m: should enter, grasping [the thigh of] one standing in water up to his navel. / Then another impartial man, with an average bow,

3.66.s:
iṣumokṣaṃ tadā kuryāddeśe tṛṇavivarjite ..
śaramokṣe same kāle nimajjetpuruṣopyasau .. 58 ..
3.66.d:
इषुमोक्षं तदा कुर्याद्देशे तृणविवर्जिते ॥
शरमोक्षे समे काले निमज्जेत्पुरुषोप्यसौ ॥ 58 ॥
3.66.m: should discharge an arrow in a place devoid of grass; / at the very time the arrow is discharged, that man should also submerge.

3.66.s:
mūrdhni vinyastapatrastu petrai caitānniveśayet ..
ādidevo'si devānāṃ śaucasyāpyāyanaṃ param .. 59 ..
3.66.d:
मूर्ध्नि विन्यस्तपत्रस्तु पेत्रै चैतान्निवेशयेत् ॥
आदिदेवोऽसि देवानां शौचस्याप्यायनं परम् ॥ 59 ॥
3.66.m: With a leaf placed upon his head, he should place these [words] upon the leaf: / "You are the primal god of gods, the supreme sustainer of purity;

3.66.s:
pañcānāṃ lokapālānāṃ tvaṃ variṣṭhaṃ jagatpate ..
trāyasvainaṃ naraṃ pāpātpaśyasi tvaṃ śubhāśubhama .. 3.328.60 ..
3.66.d:
पञ्चानां लोकपालानां त्वं वरिष्ठं जगत्पते ॥
त्रायस्वैनं नरं पापात्पश्यसि त्वं शुभाशुभम ॥ 3.328.60 ॥
3.66.m: you are the foremost of the five guardians of the world, O Lord of the universe! / Save this man from sin; you perceive good and evil!

3.66.s:
antaścarasi bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ mokṣavatsthitaḥ ..
iṣuprakṣepaṇasthānādyuvā ca balavānnaraḥ ... .. 61 ..
3.66.d:
अन्तश्चरसि भूतानां सर्वेषां मोक्षवत्स्थितः ॥
इषुप्रक्षेपणस्थानाद्युवा च बलवान्नरः ॥॥। 61 ॥
3.66.m: You move within all beings, standing as their liberation!" / And a strong young man, from the place where the arrow was shot,

3.66.s:
dhāvansa parayā śaktyā śaraṃ tatsamupātayet ..
āgate tu śaragrāhe toyasthaścenna dṛśyate .. 62 ..
3.66.d:
धावन्स परया शक्त्या शरं तत्समुपातयेत् ॥
आगते तु शरग्राहे तोयस्थश्चेन्न दृश्यते ॥ 62 ॥
3.66.m: running with his utmost strength, should bring back that arrow; / and when the arrow-fetcher returns, if the man in the water is not seen,

3.66.s:
śuddho bhavati dharmeṇa yaścāpyaṅgaṃ na darśayet ..
viṣasyātaḥ pravakṣyāmi vidhiṃ dharmyaṃ sanātanam ..63..
3.66.d:
शुद्धो भवति धर्मेण यश्चाप्यङ्गं न दर्शयेत् ॥
विषस्यातः प्रवक्ष्यामि विधिं धर्म्यं सनातनम् ॥63॥
3.66.m: he becomes pure by dharma, and also if he does not show a limb. / Next I shall proclaim the righteous, eternal rule of poison.

3.66.s:
śṛṅgiṇo vatsanābhasya himaśailodbhavasya ca..
yavāssapta pradātavyā atha vā yadghṛtāplutāḥ .. 64 ..
3.66.d:
शृङ्गिणो वत्सनाभस्य हिमशैलोद्भवस्य च॥
यवास्सप्त प्रदातव्या अथ वा यद्घृताप्लुताः ॥ 64 ॥
3.66.m: Seven barley-grains of horned vatsanābha poison originating from the snowy mountain / should be administered, or else drenched in clarified butter.

3.66.s:
mūrdhni vinyastapatrasya patre caitanniveśayet ..
tvaṃ viṣa brahmaṇaḥ putraḥ satye dharme vyavasthitaḥ . 65 ..
3.66.d:
मूर्ध्नि विन्यस्तपत्रस्य पत्रे चैतन्निवेशयेत् ॥
त्वं विष ब्रह्मणः पुत्रः सत्ये धर्मे व्यवस्थितः । 65 ॥
3.66.m: Having placed a leaf upon his head, he should place this [formula] upon the leaf: / "You, O Poison, are the son of Brahmā, established in truth and dharma!

3.66.s:
trāyasvainaṃ naraṃ pāpātsatyenāsya bhavāmṛtam ..
yena vegairvinā jīrṇaṃ chardimūrcchāvivarjitam.. 66 ..
3.66.d:
त्रायस्वैनं नरं पापात्सत्येनास्य भवामृतम् ॥
येन वेगैर्विना जीर्णं छर्दिमूर्च्छाविवर्जितम्॥ 66 ॥
3.66.m: Save this man from sin; through his truth, become nectar!" / If it is digested by him without violent fits, free from vomiting and fainting,

3.66.s:
taṃ tu śuddhaṃ vijānīyāditi dharmavido viduḥ ..
taṇḍulānāṃ pravakṣyāmi vidhiṃ dharmyaṃ sanātanam .. 67 ..
3.66.d:
तं तु शुद्धं विजानीयादिति धर्मविदो विदुः ॥
तण्डुलानां प्रवक्ष्यामि विधिं धर्म्यं सनातनम् ॥ 67 ॥
3.66.m: one should know him to be pure: so know the knowers of dharma. / I shall declare the righteous, eternal rule of the rice-grains.

3.66.s:
caurye tu taṇḍulā deyā na cānyatra kathaṃcana ..
taṇḍulānudake siktvā rātrau tatraiva sthāpayeta .. 68 ...
3.66.d:
चौर्ये तु तण्डुला देया न चान्यत्र कथंचन ॥
तण्डुलानुदके सिक्त्वा रात्रौ तत्रैव स्थापयेत ॥ 68 ॥।
3.66.m: Rice-grains are to be given in theft, and never in any other case. / Having soaked the rice-grains in water at night, he should leave them right there.

3.66.s:
taṇḍulānkārayecchuddhāñśālīnāṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ ..
mṛnmayaṃ bhājanaṃ kṛtvā savituḥ purataḥ sthitaḥ .. 69 ..
3.66.d:
तण्डुलान्कारयेच्छुद्धाञ्शालीनां पृथिवीपतिः ॥
मृन्मयं भाजनं कृत्वा सवितुः पुरतः स्थितः ॥ 69 ॥
3.66.m: The lord of the earth should have pure grains of śāli rice prepared; / placing an earthen vessel, standing before the sun,

3.66.s:
taṇḍulānmaṃtrayecśuddhānmaṃtreṇānena dharmataḥ ..
dīyate sattvadharmajñairmānuṣāṇāṃ viśodhanam ..3.328.70..
3.66.d:
तण्डुलान्मंत्रयेच्शुद्धान्मंत्रेणानेन धर्मतः ॥
दीयते सत्त्वधर्मज्ञैर्मानुषाणां विशोधनम् ॥3.328.70॥
3.66.m: he should consecrate the pure grains according to dharma with this mantra: / "This purifier of human beings is given by those who know the law of truth.

3.66.s:
tatastaṇḍula satyena dharmatastrātumarhasi ..
prabhāte kārayedeva bhakṣaṇāya na saṃśayaḥ ..71..
3.66.d:
ततस्तण्डुल सत्येन धर्मतस्त्रातुमर्हसि ॥
प्रभाते कारयेदेव भक्षणाय न संशयः ॥71॥
3.66.m: Therefore, O rice-grain, through truth you ought to save [him] according to dharma!" / At dawn he should certainly cause him to chew [them], without a doubt.

3.66.s:
trividhaḥ prāṅmukhasyeha patre niṣṭhīvayettataḥ ..
pippalasyātha bhūrjasya na tvanyasya kathaṃcana .. 72 ..
3.66.d:
त्रिविधः प्राङ्मुखस्येह पत्रे निष्ठीवयेत्ततः ॥
पिप्पलस्याथ भूर्जस्य न त्वन्यस्य कथंचन ॥ 72 ॥
3.66.m: He facing east should then spit it out three times here onto a leaf— / of the holy fig tree or of the birch tree, but never on any other.

3.66.s:
śoṇitaṃ dṛśyate yasya tamaśuddhaṃ vinirdiśet ..
athātaḥ saṃprakṣyāmi taptamāṣakanirṇayam .. 73 ..
3.66.d:
शोणितं दृश्यते यस्य तमशुद्धं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
अथातः संप्रक्ष्यामि तप्तमाषकनिर्णयम् ॥ 73 ॥
3.66.m: He in whose [spit] blood is seen, one should declare him impure. / Now therefore I shall declare the decision by the heated māṣaka coin.

3.66.s:
kārayedāyasaṃ pātraṃ tāmraṃ vā ṣoḍaśāṅgulam ..
caturaṅgulakhātaṃ tu mṛnmayaṃ vāpi kārayet .. .. 74 ..
3.66.d:
कारयेदायसं पात्रं ताम्रं वा षोडशाङ्गुलम् ॥
चतुरङ्गुलखातं तु मृन्मयं वापि कारयेत् ॥ ॥ 74 ॥
3.66.m: He should have a vessel made of iron, or of copper, sixteen aṅgulas [wide], / with a depth of four aṅgulas, or he may have it made of clay.

3.66.s:
pūrayedghṛtatailābhyāṃ palairviṃśatibhistataḥ ..
sutapte nikṣipettatra suvarṇasya tu māṣakam .. 75 ..
3.66.d:
पूरयेद्घृततैलाभ्यां पलैर्विंशतिभिस्ततः ॥
सुतप्ते निक्षिपेत्तत्र सुवर्णस्य तु माषकम् ॥ 75 ॥
3.66.m: He should fill it with twenty palas of clarified butter and oil; / when it is boiling hot, he should cast a golden māṣaka into it.

3.66.s:
vahnyaktaṃ vinyasenmantramabhiśastasya mūrdhani ..
aṅguṣṭhāṅguliyogena taptamāṣaṃ samuddharet .. 76 ..
3.66.d:
वह्न्यक्तं विन्यसेन्मन्त्रमभिशस्तस्य मूर्धनि ॥
अङ्गुष्ठाङ्गुलियोगेन तप्तमाषं समुद्धरेत् ॥ 76 ॥
3.66.m: He should place the mantra addressed to fire upon the head of the accused; / with the thumb and fingers joined, he should take out the heated māṣaka.

3.66.s:
śuddhaṃ jñeyamadagdhaṃ tu visphoṭādivivarjitam ..
phālaśuddhiṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇudhvaṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ .. 77 ..
3.66.d:
शुद्धं ज्ञेयमदग्धं तु विस्फोटादिविवर्जितम् ॥
फालशुद्धिं प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुध्वं द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥ 77 ॥
3.66.m: If unburned and free from blisters and the like, he should be known as pure. / I shall declare the purification by the ploughshare; listen, O bulls among the twice-born!

3.66.s:
āyasaṃ dvādaśapalaṃ ghaṭitaṃ phālamucyate ..
aṣṭāṅgulaṃ samaṃ dīrghaṃ caturaṃgulavistṛtam .. 78 ..
3.66.d:
आयसं द्वादशपलं घटितं फालमुच्यते ॥
अष्टाङ्गुलं समं दीर्घं चतुरंगुलविस्तृतम् ॥ 78 ॥
3.66.m: An iron ploughshare is said to be forged weighing twelve palas, / eight aṅgulas long in straight measure, and four aṅgulas wide.

3.66.s:
vahnyaktaṃ vinyasetpatramabhiśastasya mūrdhani ..
triḥ parāvartayejjihvāṃ lihatassārdhamaṅgulam .. 79 ..
3.66.d:
वह्न्यक्तं विन्यसेत्पत्रमभिशस्तस्य मूर्धनि ॥
त्रिः परावर्तयेज्जिह्वां लिहतस्सार्धमङ्गुलम् ॥ 79 ॥
3.66.m: One should place a leaf anointed with fire on the head of the accused. / He should pass his tongue three times, licking [the blade] for an inch and a half.

3.66.s:
gavāṃ kṣīraṃ pradātavyaṃ jihvāśodhanamuttamam ..
jihvāparīkṣaṇaṃ kuryāddagdhāṃ cenna vibhāvyate..3.328.80..
3.66.d:
गवां क्षीरं प्रदातव्यं जिह्वाशोधनमुत्तमम् ॥
जिह्वापरीक्षणं कुर्याद्दग्धां चेन्न विभाव्यते॥3.328.80॥
3.66.m: Cow's milk should be given as the best purifier of the tongue. / One should examine the tongue; if it is not perceived to be burned,

3.66.s:
taṃ viśuddhaṃ vijānīyādviśuddhaṃ caiva mokṣayet ..
koṣasyātha pravakṣyāmi vidhiṃ dharmyaṃ sanātanam .. 81 ..
3.66.d:
तं विशुद्धं विजानीयाद्विशुद्धं चैव मोक्षयेत् ॥
कोषस्याथ प्रवक्ष्यामि विधिं धर्म्यं सनातनम् ॥ 81 ॥
3.66.m: one should know him to be purified, and once purified, one should release him. / Now I shall declare the eternal and righteous rule of the sacred water.

3.66.s:
yoyo yāṃ devatābhaktaḥ pāyayettasya tūttaram ..
samabhaktaṃ tu devānāmādityasyaiva kārayet..82..
3.66.d:
योयो यां देवताभक्तः पाययेत्तस्य तूत्तरम् ॥
समभक्तं तु देवानामादित्यस्यैव कारयेत्॥82॥
3.66.m: Whichever deity a man is devoted to, [the judge] should make him drink the subsequent [water] of that [deity]. / But to one who is equally devoted to all deities, he should have it performed with [the water] of Āditya alone.

3.66.s:
ugrāṇāmapi devānāṃ vadhasyaiva tu dāpayet ..
sarveṣāmeva devānāṃ snāpayedāyudhaṃ svakam ..83..
3.66.d:
उग्राणामपि देवानां वधस्यैव तु दापयेत् ॥
सर्वेषामेव देवानां स्नापयेदायुधं स्वकम् ॥83॥
3.66.m: Even among terrible deities, he should give [the water] of [the deity of] destruction alone. / He should bathe the respective weapon of all the deities,

3.66.s:
snānodakaṃ vā sakalamāhareta vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
unmukhaṃ karaṇaṃ kṛtvā pāyayetprasṛtitrayam ..84..
3.66.d:
स्नानोदकं वा सकलमाहरेत विचक्षणः ॥
उन्मुखं करणं कृत्वा पाययेत्प्रसृतित्रयम् ॥84॥
3.66.m: or the wise man should collect all the bath-water. / Making his hands facing upward, he should make him drink three palmfuls,

3.66.s: idaṃ mayā naiva kṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ vāpyatha śāyinā..85..
3.66.d: इदं मया नैव कृतं कृतं वाप्यथ शायिना॥85॥
3.66.m: [with the oath]: "This was not done by me," or "Done by me while sleeping."

3.66.s:
pīte tu kośe puruṣasya dṛṣṭā devopaghātaṃ nṛpasaṃbhavaṃ vā ..
triḥsaptarātrāṃtarato nṛpeṇa bhṛśaṃ vineyaḥ puruṣaḥ sa viprāḥ..86..
3.66.d:
पीते तु कोशे पुरुषस्य दृष्टा देवोपघातं नृपसंभवं वा ॥
त्रिःसप्तरात्रांतरतो नृपेण भृशं विनेयः पुरुषः स विप्राः॥86॥
3.66.m: If, after the sacred water has been drunk, an affliction from the gods or arising from the king is seen to happen to the man / within three times seven nights, O brahmins, that man must be severely punished by the king.

3.66.s:
iti śrīviṣṇudharmottare tṛtīyakhaṇḍe mārkaṇḍeyavajrasaṃvāde munīnprati haṃsagītāsu divyapramāṇanirūpaṇaṃ nāmāṣṭāviṃśatyuttaratriśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. .. 328 ..
3.229
haṃsa uvāca ..
ekā dve ca tathā tisraścatasraśca yathākramam ..
śūdraviṭkṣatraviprāṇāṃ bhāryāḥ proktā manīṣibhiḥ .. 1 ..
śūdraiva bhāryā śūdrasya sā ca svā ca viśaḥ smṛte ..

prājāpatyastathā daivo brāhmaścāpi śubhāstrayaḥ .. 6 ..
3.66.d:
इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे तृतीयखण्डे मार्कण्डेयवज्रसंवादे मुनीन्प्रति हंसगीतासु दिव्यप्रमाणनिरूपणं नामाष्टाविंशत्युत्तरत्रिशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ ॥ 328 ॥
3.229
हंस उवाच ॥
एका द्वे च तथा तिस्रश्चतस्रश्च यथाक्रमम् ॥
शूद्रविट्क्षत्रविप्राणां भार्याः प्रोक्ता मनीषिभिः ॥ 1 ॥
शूद्रैव भार्या शूद्रस्य सा च स्वा च विशः स्मृते ॥
ते च स्वा च तथा राज्ञस्ताश्च स्वा चाग्रजन्मनः ॥ 2 ॥
न विवर्णा भवेद्भार्या कदाचिदपि कस्यचित् ॥
सवर्णैव भवेज्ज्येष्ठा असवर्णासु सत्स्वपि ॥ 3 ॥
अष्टौ विवाहा निर्दिष्टास्तेषां वक्ष्यामि लक्षणम् ॥
आहूय दानाद्ब्राह्मस्तु ऋत्विजैर्दैव उच्यते ॥ ॥ 4 ॥
गोयुगग्रहणादार्षः प्राजापत्योर्थिते तथा ॥
आसुरो द्रविणादानाद्गान्धर्वस्तु मताद्द्वयोः ॥ 9 ॥
राक्षसो युद्धहरणात्पैशाचः कन्यकाच्छलात् ॥
प्राजापत्यस्तथा दैवो ब्राह्मश्चापि शुभास्त्रयः ॥ 6 ॥

3.66.s:
gāndharvo rākṣasaścaiva madhyamau parikīrtitau ..
āsuraścaiva paiśāca ārṣaścaiva tathādhamaḥ ... .. 7 ..
na te kāryāḥ prayatnena kadācidapi kenacit ..
āsurasya tathārṣasya viśeṣo naiva vidyate .. 8 ..
śuklameva tato jñeyamalpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu..
prāṇivikrayiṇaḥ sarve narakaṃ yānti mānavāḥ....
viśeṣeṇa ca yaḥ putraṃ vikrīṇāti svakaṃ naraḥ ..
narake vasatiṃ tasya bahūnabdagaṇānviduḥ .. 3.329.10..
mṛte bhartari yā kanyā kevalaṃ hastadūṣitā ..
sā cedakṣatayoniḥ syātpunaḥ saṃskāramarhati .. 11..
ityevaṃ kecidicchanti na tanmama mataṃ dvijāḥ ....
saptame hi pade vṛtte nānyamarhati sā patim..12..
vācā dattā tu yā kanyā mantraiścaiva na saṃskṛtā..
anyasya sā bhaveddeyā sati bhartari doṣiṇī..3..
naṣṭe mṛte pravrajite klībe'tha patite patau..
pañcasvāpatsu nārīṇāṃ patiranyo vidhīyate..14..
3.66.d:
गान्धर्वो राक्षसश्चैव मध्यमौ परिकीर्तितौ ॥
आसुरश्चैव पैशाच आर्षश्चैव तथाधमः ॥॥। 7 ॥
न ते कार्याः प्रयत्नेन कदाचिदपि केनचित् ॥
आसुरस्य तथार्षस्य विशेषो नैव विद्यते ॥ 8 ॥
शुक्लमेव ततो ज्ञेयमल्पं वा यदि वा बहु॥
प्राणिविक्रयिणः सर्वे नरकं यान्ति मानवाः॥॥
विशेषेण च यः पुत्रं विक्रीणाति स्वकं नरः ॥
नरके वसतिं तस्य बहूनब्दगणान्विदुः ॥ 3.329.10॥
मृते भर्तरि या कन्या केवलं हस्तदूषिता ॥
सा चेदक्षतयोनिः स्यात्पुनः संस्कारमर्हति ॥ 11॥
इत्येवं केचिदिच्छन्ति न तन्मम मतं द्विजाः ॥॥
सप्तमे हि पदे वृत्ते नान्यमर्हति सा पतिम्॥12॥
वाचा दत्ता तु या कन्या मन्त्रैश्चैव न संस्कृता॥
अन्यस्य सा भवेद्देया सति भर्तरि दोषिणी॥3॥
नष्टे मृते प्रव्रजिते क्लीबेऽथ पतिते पतौ॥
पञ्चस्वापत्सु नारीणां पतिरन्यो विधीयते॥14॥
3.66.m:
the Gāndharva and the Rākṣasa are declared to be middling; / and the Āsura, the Paiśāca, and the Ārṣa are the lowest.
They should never be performed with effort by anyone. / There is no difference between the Āsura and the Ārṣa;
it is to be known simply as a bride-price, whether it is small or whether it is large. / All men who sell living beings go to hell; / and especially a man who sells his own son— / they know his dwelling to be in hell for a multitude of years.
When her husband has died, a maiden who was merely touched by the hand / is entitled to the sacrament again, if her virginity is intact.
Thus some desire, but that is not my opinion, O twice-born; / for when the seventh step has been completed, she is not entitled to another husband.
A maiden who has been given by word of mouth, but not consecrated with mantras, / may be given to another if the husband is found to have a defect.
When a husband is missing, dead, has renounced the world, is impotent, or has fallen from caste— / in these five misfortunes another husband is prescribed for women.

पितापितामहो भ्राता सकुल्यो जननी तथा ॥

यस्तु दोषवतीं पत्नीं सम्यक्त्वेनानुवर्त्तते ॥
दण्डयित्वा स्वशक्त्या तं समे पथि निवेशयेत्॥18॥
भर्तारं लङ्घयेद्या तु स्त्री ज्ञातिबलदर्पिता॥
तां श्वभिः खादयेद्राजा संस्थाने वध्यघातिनाम्॥19॥
भार्याया व्यभिचारिण्या परित्यागो विधीयते ॥ 3.329.20 ॥
हीनवर्णगमे चास्या वधमुक्तं मनीषिभिः ॥
भर्त्रनुज्ञां विना राजा स्त्रीणां च प्रभवेत् क्वचित् ॥ 21 ॥
अशक्तभर्तृकां नारीं शासयेत्तदनुज्ञया ॥
योन्यस्मै कन्यकां दत्त्वा भूयोन्यस्मै प्रयच्छति ॥ 22 ॥
3.66.m:
The father, paternal grandfather, brother, kinsman, and likewise the mother— / each subsequent one, if in sound mind, is the giver of the maiden upon the absence of the preceding.
He who gives away a maiden without declaring a defect / should pay two hundred [paṇas] to the king and maintain that maiden.
And whichever man calls an unblemished woman blemished through a fault, / the king should impose upon him the first violent penalty.
He who treats a defective wife as properly blameless, / [the king], having punished him according to his capacity, should set him on the right path.
A woman who defies her husband, arrogant with the power of her kinsmen, / the king should have her eaten by dogs in a place where convicts are executed.
Abandonment of an adulterous wife is ordained.
And if she has intercourse with a lower caste, execution is declared by the wise. / Without the permission of the husband, the king may have authority over women in some cases.
He should discipline a woman whose husband is incapable, with his consent. / He who, having given a maiden to one, gives her again to another—

3.66.m:
the king should fine that man a fourth part of his wealth. / When a fault arises in the husband, she should not incur punishment.
The vile man who does not approach his wife in her fertile period / should be fined a māṣaka of gold at every fertile period.
A wife who, being called, does not go to her husband during her fertile period / should be banished by the husband, having declared her fault to her mother.
The lowest of men who abandons an unblemished wife / should be fined a suvarṇa and must maintain her once again.
A man who acts unequally among his married wives / of the same caste should be fined a suvarṇa by the ruler of the earth.
A maiden, upon attaining her fertile period, should wait three years. / After the declared time, the maiden may find a suitable husband.
The maiden should not take ornaments from her father's family in a self-choice, / nor those from her mother or given by her brothers; for if she took them, it would be theft.

3.330
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
औरसः पुत्रिकापुत्रः क्षेत्रजश्च तथा परः ॥
पौनर्भवश्च कानीनः सहोढश्च तथा सुतः ॥ 1 ॥
गूढोत्पन्नो दत्तकश्च क्रीतश्चैव तथा परः ॥
अपविद्धस्तूपगतः शूद्रापुत्रस्तथैव च ॥ 2 ॥
एते द्वादश वै पुत्रास्तेषां वक्ष्यामि लक्षणम् ॥
संस्कृतायां स्वयं जातः पुत्र औरस उच्यते ॥ 3 ॥
अस्यामुत्पद्यते पुत्रो यः स मे भविता सुतः ॥
एषा दत्तापि या पित्रा पुत्रिका सा निगद्यते ॥ 4 ॥
विना वचनदत्तापि भ्रातृहीना तु पुत्रिका ॥।
तत्पुत्रः पुत्रिकापुत्रो द्वितीयः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 5 ॥
देवराद्वा सगोत्राद्वा ब्राह्मणाद्वा विचक्षणात् ॥
नियोगोत्पादितः पुत्रः क्षेत्रजः परिकीर्तितः ॥6॥।
3.66.m:
If a man does not give away a maiden who has reached puberty, even though able, that foremost of the twice-born should be punished; / he shall never have ownership over her, and by not giving away his daughter at puberty, his status as twice-born is lost.
3.330
Haṃsa said:
The son born of one's own body, the son of an appointed daughter, and next the son born of the wife; / the son of a remarried woman, the son of an unmarried girl, and likewise the son received with a bride;
the secretly born, the adopted son, and next the purchased son; / the cast-off son, the self-given son, and likewise the son of a śūdra woman—
these are indeed the twelve sons; I shall declare their characteristics. / A son born of himself upon a consecrated [wife] is called the son born of one's own body.
"The son born of her shall be my son." / Even when given away by her father, she is declared an appointed daughter.
Even given without [such] an agreement, one who is without brothers is an appointed daughter; / her son, the son of an appointed daughter, is proclaimed as the second.
Beget through appointment by a brother-in-law, a sagotra, or a learned brahmin, / the son is proclaimed as the field-born.

स्वैरिणी या पतिं हित्वा कामतोन्यं समाश्रयेत् ॥

असंस्कृतायामुत्पन्नः कानीनो भर्तुरेव सः ॥
गर्भिणी या संस्क्रियते सहोढस्तत्सुतो मतः ॥ 8 ॥
गृहे च गूढमुत्पन्नो गृहोत्पन्नः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
तस्यां सकाशात्क्रीतश्च क्रीतपुत्रो निगद्यते ॥
ताभ्यां चैवापविद्धस्तु त्वपविद्धस्तु स स्मृतः ॥9॥
विधृतो येन यस्यासौ पुत्रत्वेन निगद्यते ॥
स्वयं यश्चाभ्युपगतः पुत्रत्वे द्विजसत्तमाः॥3.330.10॥
आदौ तु पुत्रिकापुत्रः पश्चाज्जातस्त्वथौरसः ॥
औरसेन समांशस्तु तत्र स्यात्पुत्रिकासुतः॥11॥
जाते तु पुत्रिकापुत्रे क्षेत्रजोत्पादनं वृथा ॥
समाः समांशिनो ज्ञेया यादृशास्तादृशाः सुताः ॥12॥
प्रतिलोमभवाः पुत्रा न तु रिक्थस्य भागिनः ॥
धनभाग्भरणं तेषां कर्मणा कर्तुमर्हति ॥ 13 ॥
3.66.m:
She who, wanton, abandons her husband and resorts to another out of lust— / her son is proclaimed as the son of a remarried woman, the fourth.
Born of an unmarried maiden, the maiden-born son belongs to her husband alone. / She who is married while pregnant—her son is considered brought with the bride.
Born secretly in the house, he is proclaimed the secretly born. / Purchased from her presence, he is called the purchased son. / Abandoned by both of them, he is remembered as the cast-off.
He who is held by someone is spoken of as his son by adoptive taking; / and he who has offered himself for sonship, O best of twice-born!
If first there is the son of an appointed daughter and afterwards an aurasa is born, / the son of the appointed daughter would have an equal share with the aurasa.
Once the son of an appointed daughter is born, the begetting of a field-born son is futile. / Equal sons are to be known as equal sharers, such as they are.
Sons born against the grain do not share in the inheritance. / The heir of the wealth ought to provide maintenance for them according to their work.

तदपत्याः पितृवधे भागिनः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
पैतामहेन ते वित्ते स्वाम्यमर्हति केनचित् ॥ 14 ॥
जडान्धबधिरोन्मत्ता भर्तव्यास्तु निरंशकाः ॥
तेषाम्रिमृक्थहराः पुत्रा धने पैतामहे सुताः॥15॥
पतितानां न भागोस्ति तत्सुतानां च धर्मतः ॥
कर्मणः प्राक्समुत्पन्नाः पतनीयस्य ये सुताः॥16॥
तेषाम्रिक्थं प्रदातव्यं न तु ते पतिताः स्मृताः॥
प्रायश्चित्ते तथा चीर्णे पतितो भागमर्हति॥17॥
तत्पुत्रोऽपि तथा विप्रा नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
पिता चेद्विभजेत्पुत्रान्स्वेच्छा तस्य स्वके धने ॥ 18 ॥
पैतामहे त्वस्वतन्त्रः पिता भवति धर्मतः ॥
पितामहार्जिते वित्ते पितुः पुत्रस्य चोभयोः ॥ 19 ॥
स्वाम्यन्तु सदृशं ज्ञेयं पुत्रश्चेद्गुणवान्भवेत् ॥
पितुरूर्ध्वं विभजतां माताप्यंशं सुसंहरेत् ॥ 3.330.20 ॥
3.66.m:
Their offspring are proclaimed as entitled to share upon the death of the father; / in the paternal grandfather's wealth they are entitled to ownership in some measure.
The idiot, the blind, the deaf, and the insane must be maintained, having no share; / their sons who inherit the property take their share in the paternal grandfather's wealth.
According to dharma, there is no share for outcasts, nor for their sons. / But those sons who were born before the act that causes degraded status,
the inheritance must be given to them; they are not considered outcasts. / Likewise, when an expiation has been performed, the outcast is entitled to a share.
His son likewise, O brahmins; no doubt should be entertained here. / If the father should divide [the estate among] the sons, his own will prevails over his own wealth.
Over the grandfather's [wealth], however, the father is not independent according to dharma. / In wealth acquired by the grandfather, of both the father and the son
ownership is to be understood as equal, if the son is endowed with virtues. / When they divide after the father, the mother should also receive an equal share.

सवर्णास्तु सुताः सर्वे तथा ज्ञेयाः समांशिनः ॥

वैश्यापुत्रो हरेद्द्व्यंशमंशं शूद्रासुतो हरेत् ॥ 24 ॥
ब्राह्मणौ यदि पुत्रौ द्वौ चैकः शूद्रासुतो भवेत् ॥
नवधा ब्राह्मणधनं विभज्यमिति निश्चयः ॥ 25 ॥
अष्टौ ब्राह्मणयोर्भागाः शूद्रस्य नवमो भवेत् ॥
द्वौ विज्ञेयौ सुतौ स्यातामेकश्च ब्राह्मणीसुतः ॥ 26 ॥
ब्राह्मणस्वं तथा षोढा विभज्यमिति निश्चयः ॥
द्वावंशौ शूद्रयोर्देयौ चतुरोंशा हि वै द्विजाः ॥ 27 ॥
3.66.m:
All sons of the same caste are likewise to be understood as equal sharers. / A little more is to be given to the eldest; there is no doubt about this.
Even of the son of a Brāhma and Daiva [marriage], those two most venerable are equal, / [while] those born of Paiśāca and Asura [marriages] are like the son of a remarried woman.
When a brahmin has four wives, / the king should divide that wealth which is the inheritance among their sons:
The [son of a] brahmin [wife] takes four shares; the son of a kṣatriyā takes three shares; / the son of a vaiśyā takes two shares; the son of a śūdrā takes one share.
If there are two sons of a brāhmaṇī and one son of a śūdrā, / the wealth of the brahmin is to be divided into nine parts; such is the rule.
Eight shares belong to the two sons of the brāhmaṇī; the ninth belongs to the son of the śūdrā. / If there are two [śūdrā] sons, it should be known, and one son of a brāhmaṇī,
the property of the brahmin is to be divided into six parts; such is the rule. / Two shares are to be given to the two sons of the śūdrā, and four shares to the twice-born.

3.66.d:
अनेनैवानुसारेण सर्वत्रैवांशकल्पना ॥
असवर्णासु जातानां कर्तव्या पृथिवीक्षिता ॥ 28 ॥
षोढा तत्क्षत्त्रियधनं कर्तव्यमिति निश्चयः ॥
क्षत्त्रियायां ततः पुत्रा वित्ततोंशत्रयं हरेत् ॥ 29 ॥
वैश्यापुत्रो हरेद्द्व्यंशमंशं शूद्रासुतो हरेत् ॥
वैश्यास्वं तु त्रिधा कार्यं शृणु तत्रापि कल्पना ॥ 3.330.30 ॥
वैश्यापुत्रो हरेद्व्यंशमंशं शूद्रासुतो हरेत् ॥
अपुत्रस्य तु दौहित्रो रिक्थमर्हति धर्मतः॥31॥
दौहित्रस्याप्यभावे तु दुहितापि धनं हरेत्॥
तदभावे तदा भार्या तदभावे सहोदरः ॥
तस्याप्यभावे जननी तदभावे पिता हरेत् ॥
भ्रातरस्तदभावे तु भ्रातृपुत्रस्ततो हरेत् ॥ 32 ॥
सहोदरभ्रातृसुतो विद्यमाने कथंचन ॥
नान्यभ्रातृभवो भ्राता प्राप्नुयादिति निश्चयः ॥ 33 ॥
3.66.m:
In accordance with this very rule, the allotment of shares in all cases / of those born to women of different castes must be carried out by the ruler of the earth.
The wealth of a kṣatriya is to be divided into six parts; such is the rule. / Then the sons born of a kṣatriyā should take three shares of the wealth;
the son of a vaiśyā takes two shares; the son of a śūdrā takes one share. / The property of a vaiśya is to be divided into three parts; listen to the allotment in that case also:
The son of a vaiśyā takes two shares; the son of a śūdrā takes one share. / For a sonless man, however, the daughter's son is entitled to the inheritance according to dharma.
In the absence even of a daughter's son, the daughter also takes the wealth; / in her absence, then the wife; in her absence, the uterine brother; / in his absence also, the mother; in her absence, the father takes; / in his absence, the brothers; then the brother's son takes.
If a uterine brother's son exists in any way, / a brother born of another mother shall not obtain [the wealth]; such is the rule.

अन्यभ्रातृभवभ्रातुः पुत्रो यत्र व्यवस्थितः ॥
पितृव्यभ्रातृपुत्रस्तु नैव तत्र धनं हरेत् ॥ 34 ॥
अनन्तरं सपिण्डाद्यस्तस्यतस्य धनं हरेत् ॥
तदभावे सकुल्यस्य तदभावे गुरोर्भवेत् ॥ 35 ॥
शिष्यस्य तदभावे तु द्विजानां तदभावतः ॥
त्रैविद्याः समया दान्तास्तस्य वित्तस्य भागिनः ॥ 36 ॥
ब्राह्मणस्वमनाहार्यं पार्थिवानां सदा भवेत् ॥
इतरेषान्तु वर्णानां सर्वाभावे हरेन्नृपः ॥37॥
पुत्रौ तु विवदेयातां द्वाभ्यां जातौ स्त्रिया धने ॥
तयोर्यद्यस्य पित्र्यं स्यात्तत्संगृह्णीत नेतरः ॥38॥
मातृकं यद्भवेद्वित्तं कुमारीणां तु तद्भवेत् ॥
तदभावे तु सोढानां सुतानां तदभावतः ॥ 39 ॥
अध्यग्न्यध्यावनिकं दत्तं च प्रीतिकर्मणा ॥
भ्रातृमातृपितृप्राप्ते षड्विधं स्त्रीधनं स्मृतम् ॥ 3.330.40 ॥
3.66.m:
Where a son of a brother born of another mother is present, / the son of a paternal uncle's brother shall not take the wealth at all.
The next sapiṇḍa and so forth shall take the wealth of each of them; / in his absence, a sakulya; in his absence, it belongs to the guru;
in his absence, to the disciple; in his absence, to twice-born men. / Men learned in the three Vedas, self-restrained, and subdued are entitled to share that wealth.
The property of a brahmin must never be seized by kings. / For other castes, however, in the absence of all, the king shall take.
If two sons born to two [different fathers] from one woman should dispute over wealth, / whatever of the two is paternal to either, that one should take it, not the other.
Wealth that belongs to the mother belongs to the unmarried daughters; / in their absence, to the married daughters; in their absence, to the sons.
What is given before the fire, what is given at the bridal procession, and what is given as an act of affection, / and what is obtained from a brother, mother, or father—strīdhana is remembered as sixfold.

3.66.m:
That which is [received] in the Brāhma, Daiva, Ārṣa, Gāndharva, and Prājāpatya [marriages], / if she dies without issue, is desired for the husband alone.
[While that received] in other [forms] goes to the father […] wealth […] should be. / An ornament which has been worn by women while the husband was alive,
the co-heirs must not divide; if they divide it, they become degraded. / If among brothers born of the same father one should have a son,
all of them are made possessed of a son through that son; such is the sacred tradition. / If among all co-wives one should have a son,
all of them are proclaimed possessed of sons through that son. / What has been acquired by one's own effort without detriment to the ancestral property
What was obtained through one's own effort, he is not obliged to give against his will.
If the eldest or youngest among them is deprived of his share through the distribution of portions,
or if another dies, his share is not lost.
Brothers born of the same womb, gathering together, shall divide it equally,

3.66.m:
as well as the brothers who have reunited and sisters of the same caste.
When the wealth has been divided, those born afterward take the father's property alone.
Or else, a share must be given to him by those who have already divided, in proportion to their shares,
after giving a share in due order according to their own portion.
Unmarried maiden daughters must likewise be given sacraments by those who have divided.
Where wealth is left behind after the division has been made,
a division must be made there according to what was stated earlier.
Clothing, a vehicle, an ornament, cooked food, water, women,
and during the performance of religious and secular tasks, and a book, are not to be divided.
The heir who takes the inheritance shall pay the debt and he alone shall offer the funerary ball.
He should support all those who ought to be supported by him—such is my opinion.
The heir taking the inheritance who does not perform the rites for the deceased according to rule,
the king should swiftly banish that thief from his own realm.
O brahmins, whenever someone's property falls to the king,
